providers.holdingsNote: RECORDED, NOT HARVESTED, and that is a weaker claim. irishgenealogy.ie sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that answers 403 to anything but a human's browser, so this list is written from the site's own published description of what it holds rather than read off the page. Treat the diocesan coverage as the shape of the thing and check the live page before relying on a specific year. See data/_declined.json for why it was not scraped.

providers.name: IstriaNet
providers.what: A volunteer-built reference on Istria — history, bibliography and the AMSI series index. Worked by the Defranceski archive for the bibliography of Camillo De Franceschi's writings. A guide to where the scholarship is, not a register. Not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: JewishGen

providers.name: Kansallisarkisto / HisKi

providers.name: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár (Hungarian National Archives)
providers.what: The archives of the Kingdom of Hungary, which until 1920 meant Slovakia, Transylvania, the Banat and Croatia as well. Civil registration duplicates from 1895 are here even where the ground is now in another country.

providers.name: Žrtve rata 1941–1945 — Muzej žrtava genocida
providers.what: The Museum of Genocide Victims in Belgrade's name-by-name register of people killed in Yugoslavia between 1941 and 1945 — 659,122 records, free and without an account. Searchable by given name, surname, year of birth, the MUNICIPALITY AND PLACE OF RESIDENCE ON 6 APRIL 1941, and by place, year and circumstances of death; each row also carries the parent's name, place of birth and nationality as recorded. That pre-war residence field is what makes it genealogical rather than commemorative: it places a named person in a named village on a fixed date, which is exactly what a register would give you and often the only thing that survives for these years. Counted as an INDEX — it gives structured records, not images of the documents behind them. Scope is the whole of the former Yugoslavia; the countries listed here are the ones seen in the data (Vukovar and Vinkovci, Zavidovići and Lopare, Sremska Mitrovica), so it will also answer for Montenegro and North Macedonia beyond what has been checked here. The interface is Serbian. Read from the site itself on 2026-09-29; access class confirmed by use, not assumed. HOW TO SEARCH IT WITHOUT READING A FAMILY AS ABSENT. The surname field matches EXACTLY, not as a substring: «Franceschi» returns 0 while «Defranceschi» returns 2, so a stem finds nothing and every prefixed form has to be sent as its own query. And the spellings are not interchangeable — they hold DIFFERENT PEOPLE. «Defranceschi» gives two men at Pula and Vodnjan; «Defrančeški» gives a third at Pazin and Gologorica, and neither query returns the other's records. Query the Italian, the Croatian and the diacritic-stripped forms separately and treat the results as additive. Verified by search on 2026-09-29. One more thing worth knowing: the front end races when queries are run back to back, and can paint one query's rows under another's count, so a count is only trustworthy taken one query per page load.
providers.triageNote: Homepage and result grid read directly; 659,122 records reported by the site's own paging.

providers.name: MyHeritage
providers.what: Commercial, with a large tree network and good European newspaper and directory coverage. Search is free; opening a record is not. A LINK CHECKER CANNOT TELL YOU WHETHER A MYHERITAGE CITATION IS ALIVE, measured 2026-10-09 against 428 of them carried into a family archive from a GEDCOM export. Record pages answer an unauthenticated request in one of two ways, and NEITHER IS AN HONEST 200: either a 302 to a door, or HTTP 200 WITH AN 843-BYTE BODY READING «Request unsuccessful. Incapsula incident ID: …». A checker that reads the status code alone therefore reports every one of them as RESOLVING. Any archive auditing its outward citations has to read the body, and should grade these neither alive nor dead.

providers.name: Archives State Agency
providers.what: The State Agency «Архиви» itself — the body that runs the Central State Archives, the military-historical archive at Veliko Tarnovo and all 26 regional state archives. Start here: the digital archive searches every branch from one box. All of Bulgaria's state archives are branches of one body, the State Agency «Архиви», on one site, and the terms are the same for all of them. The free DIGITAL ARCHIVE («ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ») searches each archive separately and returns described items with a full citation — archive > fond > опис > архивна единица > лист — and the image with them. It is a SELECTION, in the hundreds per archive, not a bulk scan of registers. Fond lists and finding aids are published per archive. THE REGISTERS ARE MOSTLY NOT HERE, AND THE REASON IS A LAW: civil registration began on 1 January 1893, the municipality writes the registers and KEEPS THEM FOR 130 YEARS before transferring them to the state archive, so until that term runs out certified copies come from the municipality of birth or residence, not from the archive. Two more doors the agency names itself: it CANNOT certify Bulgarian origin — that is the Executive Agency for Bulgarians Abroad, with citizenship at the Ministry of Justice — and service in the Bulgarian army is checked only by the Държавен военноисторически архив at Veliko Tarnovo.
providers.triageNote: Surveyed 2026-10-09; one survey covers all 28 agency archives, which share a site and a policy. www.archives.government.bg opens with no account asked for. Its ДИГИТАЛЕН АРХИВ form posts to /search.php with an archive id, and a keyword search returns «Показани резултати: N» with thumbnails under /illustrations/ and the citation path «фонд > опис > а.е. > лист»; «Пловдив» in archive 16 returned 86. Each archive page carries Фондове, Фондообразуватели, Архивни справочници, Пътеводители, Списък на фондове and Уникални и особено ценни документи. The «Услуги и използване» page states the 130-year rule: «Актовете по гражданско състояние … се съставят от общината … и се съхраняват в нея 130 години, след което се предават в съответния държавен архив, съгласно чл. 85, ал. 3 от Закона за гражданската регистрация», and that until then «заверени преписи и копия се издават от съответната община». NOT REACHED: the agency documents free access to the digitised Exarchate parish registers «чрез Информационната система на държавните архиви (ИСДА) на адрес: http://isda.archives.government.bg:84/FundSearch.aspx» — isda.archives.government.bg resolves to 212.122.187.196 and timed out on ports 84, 8081, 80 and 443, over http and https, to curl and to a real browser. The same address is behind the site's «Е-УСЛУГИ» link. Recorded as unreachable from here, not as closed.

providers.name: Central State Archives of Bulgaria
providers.what: Централен държавен архив, Sofia — archive id 28, and the one Bulgarian archive with a register series that matters to people outside the country. It holds the ENORIYSKI REGISTRI, the parish registers of the Bulgarian population under the spiritual jurisdiction of the Bulgarian Exarchate in Constantinople across the European Ottoman lands — Eastern (Adrianople) and Western (Aegean) Thrace, and Southern (Aegean), Western (Vardar) and Northern (Pirin) Macedonia. They carry named individuals and count as proof of Bulgarian origin. READ THE DATE CAREFULLY: they were compiled in 1906–1907, so they record only people born before or during those years. The digitised part — fond 246К, inventories 9 and 10 — is FREE, through the state archives' information system ИСДА, which did not answer from here. The CSA also answers enquiries about Bulgarian refugees from Thrace and Macedonia, given full name, place and year of birth, and the settlement they were resettled in. Its own slice of the digital archive answered «снимка» with 70 items.

providers.name: SS. Cyril and Methodius National Library
providers.what: Св. св. Кирил и Методий, the national library in Sofia — and for anyone tracing Bulgarian or Macedonian families BEFORE 1893 this is a better door than the state archives. Its digital library is free «в пълния им обем», and two of its collections are the Ottoman-era equivalents of parish registers: the ДЕФТЕРИ — Ottoman tax and population registers, which list householders village by village — and the СИДЖИЛИ, the kadı court registers. Beside them sit the Oriental documents, Eastern and Slavonic manuscripts, early printed books, and BULGARIAN NEWSPAPERS AND MAGAZINES 1844–1944. The Oriental Collections department alone holds about a million sheets in 342,000 archival units covering the 15th to the early 20th century, in Ottoman Turkish, Arabic and Persian, plus 4,000 manuscript codices and 2,000 volumes of early printed books. There is also the Български исторически архив — personal and institutional papers, with its photographs digitised separately. The catalogue is COBISS, at bg.cobiss.net. This is a legal-deposit library and a separate institution from the State Agency «Архиви»; its terms are its own.

providers.what: Immigration and naturalisation files, service records and alien registration — including the wartime files of European arrivals. NO DEEP LINK IS POSSIBLE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Tried on 2026-09-30: RecordSearch runs on a server session and says so itself — «you are no longer in an active session… a link or bookmark referred to an expired session… RecordSearch requires cookies to be enabled to store a session identifier». A URL carrying a surname cannot be handed to somebody; it lands them on an expiry notice rather than a result. So this row deliberately has no `deepLink` where Cognomix and others do, and anything that wants to send a reader here has to send them to the search screen to type it themselves. Access is genuinely free — the site offers «search as a guest» without an account — which is why it stays `free`.

providers.name: NAAIRS — National Archives of South Africa
providers.what: The South African archives index — estate files above all, which are the backbone of South African genealogy. An index; the file is ordered from the depot. TWO DATABASES SINCE THE 2026 MIGRATION AND ONLY ONE IS COMPLETE: NARSSA's own 'Using the Search Function' page states it is migrating more than 8.3 million entries from the old NAAIRS database to the new one, that the new 'fulltext search' WILL NOT DISPLAY ALL THE RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM, and that 'Search Old NAAIRS database' will provide a more complete search. Both are offered to the public side by side. A NIL FROM THE NEW DATABASE IS THEREFORE NOT A NIL, and any recorded NAAIRS negative should say which database answered and at what address. *** AND AS OF 11 OCTOBER 2026 THE COMPLETE ONE HAS AN ADDRESS AND A NAME: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.za/search/, the “NATIONAL ARCHIVAL INFORMATION SEARCH SYSTEM” (page title NarsaSearchPortal). *** NARSSA's own notice still carries the 8.3-million migration warning AND ENDS “To search the complete database please click on: Search NAAIRS Database”, WHOSE LINK IS THAT URL — so the “Search Old NAAIRS database” a reader goes looking for is this portal, not a separate legacy address. THE OLD SEARCH MANAGER ENDPOINT www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl IS DEAD (503 over http, timeout over https) and naairs.htm is 404; the service has now moved twice in a month, so DATE EVERY NAAIRS NEGATIVE AND RECORD THE URL. HOW IT WORKS: free, no account, an Angular app covering ALL TWENTY REPOSITORIES — ECKAR, GEN (the Genealogical Society's gravestone data), HER, KAB, LAR, MAN, NAB, NAR, NCAR, NFVSA, NWAR, OVM, ROS, RSA (all of them at once), SAB, TAB, TBD, TBE, TBK, VAB — with a four-keyword Contains/AND/OR form and a year range. Underneath it POSTs JSON to /search-api/api/search as {repositoryCode, keywords:[{keyword, operator, matchType, enabled}], hasDigitalObject, startComparand, endComparand, sortBy, page, limit} and returns {total, results[], facets}. THREE TRAPS. (1) THE APP'S OWN ROUTES 404 IF TYPED DIRECTLY — there is no server-side fallback, so a deep link cannot be shared and the portal must be entered at /search/ with the repository then clicked. (2) A MULTI-WORD KEYWORD IS NOT A PHRASE: two surnames in one box returned more records than either alone. One surname per box. (3) Run a control: SMITH returns 47,936 and SCHMIDT 3,418 across RSA, so a zero from a working search looks nothing like a zero from a broken one.

providers.name: National Archives of Ireland
providers.what: What survived 1922 and what was rebuilt since — the 1901 and 1911 censuses in full and free, Tithe Applotment books, wills and the census fragments recovered from other collections.

providers.name: National Archives of the Philippines
providers.what: Holds the Spanish-era civil and notarial records and, crucially for Filipino genealogy, the 1849 Catálogo alfabético de apellidos — the decree that assigned surnames by town and is why a Filipino surname often names a province. Answers 403 to a script; opens for a person. Harvested and its address opened, nothing more: what it holds, what is online and what it costs to look are unchecked here.

providers.name: National Archives Catalog (NARA)
providers.what: The US National Archives catalogue and scans — naturalisations, passenger lists, military service, land.

providers.name: Nationaal Archief
providers.what: The Dutch National Archives at The Hague. WieWasWie pools the civil registration indexes of every regional archive and is the usual way in; this is the institution behind the national series — the colonial, military, notarial and VOC material that no index of births and deaths reaches.

providers.name: National Historical Commission of the Philippines
providers.what: The commission's own holdings and its published local histories, which are often the only account of a town's records. Answers 403 to a script; opens for a person. Harvested and its address opened, nothing more: what it holds, what is online and what it costs to look are unchecked here.

providers.name: Нацыянальны гістарычны архіў Беларусі (NIAB)
providers.what: The National Historical Archives of Belarus, Minsk — the holder of the pre-Soviet Belarusian record. OPENED 2026-09-29, and the front page carries a fact worth more than any catalogue entry: BIOGRAPHICAL RESEARCH REQUESTS FROM PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS WERE SUSPENDED ON 17.09.2026 because of the backlog, and the reading room requires an appointment booked in advance. A letter sent now is not being taken. Check whether that has lifted before planning around it. Until today Belarus's only source in this atlas was POLAND's archive portal, correct for the old Kresy Wschodnie and silent on Minsk and everything east.
providers.triageNote: Named from Wikidata; homepage read directly on 2026-09-29 except where the row says otherwise.

providers.name: National Library of Ireland — Catholic Parish Registers
providers.what: Every surviving Irish Catholic parish register to 1880, photographed and free. Browse only — no index.

providers.name: National Library of the Philippines
providers.what: Holds Filipiniana and microfilmed parish registers alongside the national collection. Harvested and its address opened, nothing more: what it holds, what is online and what it costs to look are unchecked here.

providers.name: National Records of Scotland
providers.what: The archive behind ScotlandsPeople. Kirk session records, sasines, services of heirs and the estate papers — the Scottish sources that are not births, marriages and deaths.

providers.name: NSK digitalna — Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica
providers.what: The National and University Library in Zagreb's digital portal: Croatian newspapers and periodicals, browsable and free. ANNO covers this ground in German for the Habsburg years; this is the Croatian-language press, which is where a family is named in its own language. The oldest run — Stare hrvatske novine — is served from dnc.nsk.hr over http, which the portal links to; the portal itself is https and is the entry point recorded here. The newspaper archive itself is listed separately as nsk-stare-novine.

providers.name: Stare hrvatske novine (NSK)
providers.what: Stare hrvatske novine — the National and University Library in Zagreb's digitised Croatian newspaper runs, the oldest of them, browsable by title and year. Its sibling row nsk-digitalna is the same library's wider digital portal and links here; this is the newspaper archive itself, listed separately because it is served from its own host and is what a reader is told to open. Worked by the Defranceski archive for «Galeb» and «Kvarner», the two Bakar papers. A newspaper is not a register, but it dates a family to a town when no register survives. Access not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Archivinformationssystem (Österreichisches Staatsarchiv)
providers.what: The Austrian State Archives' own finding aid, searchable by field. Worked by the Defranceski archive, which also recorded that the default search operator hides results — a search here needs its operator set deliberately. A catalogue, not images. Not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: OpenStarts (Università di Trieste)
providers.what: The University of Trieste's open repository. Worked by the Defranceski archive, which OCR'd and read the 1869 «Guida schematica di Trieste» — a city directory, which names householders street by street in years no register covers. Not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: PARES
providers.what: The Spanish archives portal — strongest on emigration to the Americas and on military and colonial service.

providers.name: Porta fontium
providers.what: A Bavarian–Czech joint portal. Parish registers of western Bohemia, free.

providers.name: PRONI — Public Record Office of Northern Ireland
providers.what: The record office for the six counties, and the reason Ulster research is not as badly burnt as the rest of Ireland: PRONI held copies and estate papers that were never in the Four Courts. Church records, wills, valuation revision books.

providers.name: Queensland Historical BDM Index
providers.what: Queensland's historical births, deaths and marriages index. Free to search; certificates are charged. Every Australian state runs its own.

providers.name: Raduraksti — Latvian State Historical Archives
providers.what: Latvia's church registers, revision lists and the 1935 census, scanned. A free account, and the Baltic German Lutheran registers of Livonia and Courland are the bulk of it.

providers.name: Mi Registro Civil
providers.what: Mexico's Plataforma Nacional del Registro Civil. OPENED 2026-09-29, AND IT IS NOT A GENEALOGICAL SOURCE — worth saying plainly, because its name promises one. It is a SERVICES portal: you pick one of the 32 entidades from a dropdown (Aguascalientes through Zacatecas, plus EXTRANJERO) and it shows the trámites that state offers — ordering a certified copy of a civil record, and checking the status of a request you already made. There is no historical search, no index to browse and no images. Mexican civil registration is administered per state, and this is the front door to thirty-two separate state offices rather than a national record set. Filed as `catalogue` because that is the nearest true class — the paper is not photographed and must be asked for — though even a catalogue is more than it offers.
providers.triageNote: Homepage opened and its own form read on 2026-09-29

providers.name: Российский государственный архив древних актов (RGADA)
providers.what: The Russian State Archive of Ancient Acts — pre-1917 fonds, the deepest of the Russian state collections and the one a genealogist working before the revolution is sent to. Named and located from its own Wikidata item; NOT yet opened, so no claim is made here about what a visitor can reach.
providers.triageNote: Named from Wikidata; homepage read directly on 2026-09-29 except where the row says otherwise.

providers.name: Riksarkivet — Digitala forskarsalen
providers.what: The Swedish National Archives. Much is now free; the highest-quality parish register images are on the commercial ArkivDigital.

providers.name: Indeks — Hrvatsko rodoslovno društvo
providers.what: A Croatian genealogical index, run by the genealogical society. Its robots.txt names this class of agent and refuses it, so this atlas links to it and does not read it — see data/_declined.json.

providers.name: Rigsarkivet — Arkivalieronline
providers.what: The Danish National Archives. Parish registers and censuses, free.

providers.name: Saaga — Estonian National Archives
providers.what: Estonia's parish registers, revision lists and soul lists, photographed and free. Lutheran registers in German, Orthodox in Russian, and the 19th-century revision lists that name a whole household at once.

providers.name: ScotlandsPeople
providers.what: The official Scottish records — statutory registers, old parish registers, censuses and wills. Pay-per-view credits, and the only lawful route to most of it.

providers.name: SIAN — Sistema de Informações do Arquivo Nacional
providers.what: The Arquivo Nacional's own catalogue, and the thing worth linking rather than the institution's front page: it is where a fonds is looked up. An index, not images.

providers.name: SIRAnet
providers.what: The Slovenian regional archives' shared catalogue. Largely a finding aid — it tells you the book exists and where it is.

providers.name: Stadtarchiv Reutlingen
providers.what: The municipal archive of Reutlingen, including its photograph database. Worked by the Defranceski archive. Not yet surveyed.
providers.triageNote: Unreachable 2026-10-09. stadtarchiv.reutlingen.de returned nothing to curl — no status, no bytes. Row stays unsurveyed.

providers.name: Szukaj w Archiwach
providers.what: The Polish state archives' scans, free and without an account. Covers ground now in Ukraine, Belarus and Lithuania as well as Poland. *** BUT IT IS BOT-GATED AND A SCRIPT CANNOT READ IT. *** On 11 October 2026 every request to szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl — the search API and the plain search page alike — returned a 212-byte Incapsula challenge page with “robots: noindex,nofollow” and nothing else. FREE TO A PERSON IN A BROWSER, CLOSED TO ANYTHING AUTOMATED, and this atlas records that rather than working around it. It matters because this is the national catalogue: it is the instrument that answers “does this fonds exist and where is it”, which the sibling portal Genealogia w Archiwach cannot do, so a question that ought to take one query becomes a letter to an archive.

providers.name: Torre do Tombo / Digitarq
providers.what: The Portuguese national archive's scans, free. District archives publish parish registers through the same system.

providers.name: Trove
providers.what: The National Library of Australia's newspaper and gazette archive. Free and full-text. Most titles stop at 1954 for copyright, which is the usual rule of thumb — BUT TWO EXCEPTIONS REACH MUCH LATER AND ARE EASY TO MISS: THE CANBERRA TIMES IS DIGITISED 1926-1995, and the COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA GAZETTE 1901-1973, whose naturalisation and citizenship lists carry name, street address and date. Those two make Trove usable for post-war arrivals that the 1954 rule would rule out. NOTE THAT THE SEARCH NORMALISES SPELLING — two different spellings of one surname can return an identical result set — SO TROVE CANNOT BE USED AS A SPELLING TEST. The v3 API needs an X-API-KEY header and does not serve article text at ordinary key level; the public article page carries the OCR.

providers.name: WieWasWie / Open Archieven
providers.what: The Dutch civil registration indexes, pooled from every regional archive. Free, and unusually complete.

providers.name: WikiTree
providers.what: A free, single shared tree with an unusually strong sourcing culture. Not a record source.

providers.name: Yad Vashem — Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names
providers.what: Names and testimony pages for victims of the Shoah, free, no account. THE SEARCH IS FULLY URL-DRIVEN even though the site is an Angular app: /en/names/search-results-names?page=N&gn_last_name=X&gnt_last_name=yvSynonym&gn_first_name=Y&gnt_first_name=yvSynonym, with gnt_ taking yvSynonym, literal or soundex. THE RESULTS COME IN THREE TABS AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE ALMOST NOBODY USES: “Results Regarding Victims”, “RESULTS REGARDING DATA SUBMITTERS” (append #submitter to the URL) and “Additional Results”. The submitter tab lists every record whose SUBMITTER matched the name searched — so SEARCHING A SURVIVOR'S NAME THERE RETURNS THE DEAD HE WROTE DOWN, and one Page of Testimony can be turned into a whole family in a single query. There are also Submitter Last Name and Submitter First Name fields in the advanced form for the same purpose. TWO THINGS MEASURED IN USE. (1) THE SYNONYM EXPANSION IS LOOSE and will fold in a different submitter of a similar name from another country — in one test, 24 of 29 results belonged to somebody else and had to be separated by place — so a submitter set must be READ and not counted. (2) A PAGE OF TESTIMONY IS A RELATIONSHIP DOCUMENT, NOT A DATE DOCUMENT. Written from memory, often decades later and often in Hebrew and auto-translated back, it is the best evidence there is for who was whose son and the worst for when: in one family read here a Page disagreed with the German federal memorial list on a birth day AND a death year (the lists were right both times), two Pages by the same man for the same victim gave two different places of death, and the same parents appeared under German forenames on one form and Hebrew ones on the other — which is itself a gift, because it hands you the Hebrew names a community register would use. What a Page gives that no list gives is the single word in the “relationship to victim” field: son, nephew, grandson.

providers.name: Cognomix — Mappe dei cognomi italiani
providers.what:
Cognomix — where an Italian surname is, by region. OPENED 2026-09-29 on /mappe-dei-cognomi-italiani/FORNASAR, which reports «circa 25 famiglie Fornasar in Italia» and breaks it down: Piemonte 11, Friuli V.G. 8, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1, drawn on a Leaflet map of Italy. Free, no account, and the URL takes the surname uppercased, so a page can be linked to directly.
WHAT IT COUNTS IS FAMILIES TODAY, NOT RECORDS. This is the Italian equivalent of the national-register rows this atlas already holds for Croatia, Slovenia and France — «how many people of that name a state counted», the closest thing to «where the name is now» — and the same caveat applies twice over: it says nothing about where a family was in 1780, and a small number tells you as much about the source as about the name. It is an INDEX, not images: there is no register behind it to open.
The page carries heavy third-party advertising, which is worth knowing before sending somebody there but says nothing about the data.
providers.triageNote: Opened on a real surname page (FORNASAR) on 2026-09-29; the distribution and its per-region counts read directly off the page.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku
providers.what: The state archive of Dubrovnik, in the Sponza palace, holding the records of the Republic of Ragusa, which was its own state until 1808 and kept its own chancery. IMPORTANT, AND THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: it NO LONGER HOLDS THE PARISH REGISTERS. A senior archivist there wrote on 28 September 2026 that «Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku predao je sve matične knjige Biskupskom ordinarijatu u Dubrovniku» — all the matične knjige have gone to the Diocesan Ordinariate — and referred the enquiry on. So a register question addressed here is answered with a redirect, and the Republic's own pre-1808 fonds is what this institution is still for.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive after a reply from the archive itself. Access class not surveyed. NOTE the atlas's existing asd-ragusa is the Archivio di Stato di RAGUSA IN SICILY, on Antenati — not this. Ragusa is the Italian name of Dubrovnik and the two are a standing trap.

providers.name: Arhiv Dubrovačke biskupije (Biskupski ordinarijat)
providers.what: The diocesan archive of Dubrovnik, and SINCE THE TRANSFER THE HOLDER OF THE CITY'S PARISH REGISTERS: the state archive states it handed over all the matične knjige and gives this as the address for them. Contact arhiv@db.hr, telephone 020 324 913, both as given by the state archive on 28 September 2026. Nothing has been asked of it yet, and no statement about what it holds volume by volume, what it charges, or whether it answers by email, is made here — only that it is where the registers went.
providers.triageNote: Recorded ONLY on the state archive's own referral, not from the diocese. Its holdings, access and whether it replies are all unsurveyed. Wikidata id not looked up.

providers.name: HDA — Pretraga matičnih knjiga (HR-HDA-1448)
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives' own searchable index of HR-HDA-1448, «Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji» — registers of ALL confessions across Croatia, plus Bosnian Catholics, from the mid-16th to the first half of the 20th century, microfilmed from originals held in state archives, church archives, parish offices, registry offices and monasteries. This answers «is this parish filmed at all» in one query, which arhinet's own row cannot: three drop-downs (parish/regiment, confession, type), then Pretraži. A row gives the period, PRIJEPIS when it is a transcript rather than the original, the holding institution, the signatura svitka (e.g. ZM-34C/681), the topografska oznaka (e.g. M-1278) and Digitalni oblik Da/Ne. Types: R births, V marriages, U deaths, S status animarum, Z confirmations, O anniversarii, I index. To order: info@arhiv.hr with place, type, period, signatura and topografska oznaka; consulted in the HDA reading room in Zagreb, max ten units a day. TWO TRAPS. First, the place box is a Telerik combo on an ASP.NET page: setting it FROM SCRIPT changes only what it displays and never commits to the server, so the search runs on an empty place and returns «Nema zapisa za pregled» — identical to a real nil. On 2026-09-29 that manufactured nine false negatives in one sitting, caught only by re-running a known-positive place as a control and watching it come back empty too. Always run that control. Second, the site itself warns that one settlement may be listed under several name forms — CRIKVENICA has four — so check every variant before calling a place absent.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive after using it to settle whether one Lika parish was filmed. Free and needs no login; access class 'index' because it indexes holdings rather than serving images — nothing in HR-HDA-1448 was found digitised for the parish tested.

providers.name: HR-HDA-883 — Zbirka matičnih knjiga (Hrvatski državni arhiv)
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives' own collection of ORIGINAL parish registers — distinct from HR-HDA-1448, which is microfilm of registers held elsewhere, and from the register search at provider hda-mk-search, which indexes 1448 and not this. Covers parishes of the Zagreb archdiocese, the Đakovo-Srijem and SENJ-MODRUŠ dioceses, Orthodox parishes of the Gornji Karlovac eparchy, and others. A published inventory lists it parish by parish with date ranges: Angelika Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu», Arhivski vjesnik 60 (2017), 251-311, https://hrcak.srce.hr/194831. A machine-readable extract of those holdings exists — 2,503 volumes across 357 parishes, 1585-1947, as parish/confession/type/date-range — held by the Defranceschi family archive and available on request. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT COMMITTED HERE: this atlas's own licence gate is right that a dataset dropped into data/ becomes something the atlas must publish and disclose on /data/, and whether to take on a source with no stated publisher licence is the atlas's decision, not a contributing archive's. THE DATE CUT IS THE IMPORTANT THING AND IT IS NOT ARBITRARY: a decision of the NRH Ministry of the Interior of 13 May 1949 required every register with entries UP TO 1860 to be handed to the competent archive, while those from 1860 onward stayed with the state registry offices that needed them in daily work. So a parish that appears here ending in 1858 has not stopped keeping records — anything after 1860 is simply somewhere else, normally the matični ured or the parish. That single rule explains a great many apparent gaps across Croatia.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive. access 'onsite': the originals are consulted on paper in the HDA reading room; no online images are known to this row. An extract of the printed inventory exists but is NOT committed here — see the description. It is a conservative parse and undercounts: it reads only «MKR 1789.–1833.» forms, so single-year and index entries are missing, about 2,503 of 3,017 candidate lines.

providers.name: Queensland State Archives
providers.what: Queensland's state archive. ArchivesSearch is an item-level catalogue, free and open, covering court, lands, immigration, police and school records. VERIFIED IN USE: the series Supreme Court (Northern) Ecclesiastical Files (Wills) S6220 alone holds 15,707 items, named per person, each marked open access. Catalogue only — the files themselves are paper and must be ordered or viewed on site; a catalogue entry gives the name, a year and an item ID and nothing more. A usable JSON endpoint exists at /api/fetch?uri=/repositories/2/archival_objects/<id>, which returns the full record including its series and preferred citation. The /api/search endpoint is live but its free-text parameter was not established: type[] is accepted and every text parameter tried was rejected. Trove indexes a subset of these item records, so they can also be reached from there.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Mazza Family archive after reading item records through both the /api/fetch endpoint and Trove. Access class is catalogue on the evidence of the catalogue itself; what an ordinary visitor pays to ORDER a file has not been surveyed.

providers.name: City of Cape Town — City Parks, cemeteries and burial registers
providers.what: The municipality that HOLDS THE ORIGINAL burial registers for about forty Cape Town cemeteries, Maitland (Woltemade) among them — FamilySearch's Cape cemetery collection names it as the location of the originals. NO ONLINE RECORD SEARCH WAS FOUND: the cemetery pages advertise burials, cremations, exhumations and grave reservations, and list telephone numbers, with nothing said about historical registers or genealogy enquiries. So this is a WRITE-OR-TELEPHONE source, not a searchable one. WHAT IS ONLINE INSTEAD is FamilySearch collection 2790463, 'South Africa, Cape, Cemetery Records 1872-2011', about 41,900 images of these same registers, digitised from the City's own Cape Metro Cemetery Records — and REDACTED: the cause-of-death column is blacked out, so the City's own copy holds something the digitisation does not.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Lerena archive, which read two openings of the Maitland Road Cemetery Record of Interments on 8 October 2026. ACCESS CLASS STILL NEEDS A PERSON: the homepage was fetched and the FamilySearch collection page read, and nothing was ordered, telephoned or paid for, so 'unsurveyed' is the honest class. The Wikidata id is the metropolitan municipality, which is the body that holds the records; there is no separate item for City Parks.

providers.name: Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru / National Library of Wales
providers.what: Aberystwyth. The legal deposit library for Wales. Its own navigation names four digital collections — TITHE MAPS, NEWSPAPERS, JOURNALS and the CATALOGUE. The newspaper service is WELSH NEWSPAPERS ONLINE at newspapers.library.wales, advertised as free and covering 1804–1919, which is the run that matters for Welsh families whose notices are otherwise only on subscription sites. NOT YET SURVEYED: what an ordinary visitor can actually retrieve was not established on this visit, because the newspaper service did not open (see the triage note). The main site at library.wales is open and needs no account to browse.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, 2026-10-09, while looking for a free copy of a Caernarvon & Denbigh Herald obituary of 1843. A NATIONAL LIBRARY THE ATLAS DID NOT LIST: before this row, the only providers covering Wales were Findmypast and the GRO, both paid. REACHED: www.library.wales loaded normally. NOT REACHED: newspapers.library.wales returned a Cloudflare «Performing security verification» interstitial that did not clear in about forty seconds, on a search URL and again on the bare homepage. It was NOT worked around. That is one browser on one day and is not an access class — the interstitial clears for most visitors — so access stays «unsurveyed» until somebody gets in and says what is free.

providers.name: The Gazette (London, Edinburgh and Belfast)
providers.what: The official journal of record of the United Kingdom, free and full-text searchable back to 1665, with no account. THREE EDITIONS — London, Edinburgh and Belfast — and the same notice is frequently printed in two of them days apart, which is a free second reading of the SAME TEXT UNDER DIFFERENT OCR. A gazette names ordinary people no register indexes: army and navy commissions and every promotion, colonial and civil appointments, insolvencies and bankruptcies, naturalisations, changes of name, partnerships dissolved, probate and estate notices. Verified 2026-10-09 by reconstructing a career from Ensign in 1837 to the government of a colony in 1859 out of ten notices, for a man previously known only from two index entries.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, 2026-10-09. TWO OPERATIONAL FACTS, BOTH MEASURED. (1) THE OCR MANGLES NAMES AND THE SEARCH IS OVER THE OCR: one man appears as «Qeorge», «Greorge» and «D'Aroy» across his own notices, so a surname search misses most of a career and the thing to search is whichever token is least corruptible — an unusual middle name beat both his forename and his surname. (2) A MULTI-WORD QUERY COMBINED WITH A DATE RANGE RETURNS HTTP 500 and redirects to a sign-in page, which looks like a paywall and is not one; a single token with a date range, or a quoted phrase without one, both work. An apostrophe in the query does the same.

providers.name: FIBIS — Families in British India Society
providers.what: Over two million names for the British in India, transcribed by volunteers, with a stated policy that the data be free to all comers; a small number of files are members-only. MUCH OF IT IS INDEXED FROM THE BRITISH LIBRARY'S INDIA OFFICE RECORDS, published with the IOR's permission — including the Index of Ecclesiastical returns for Bombay, Bengal and Madras marriages, baptisms and burials. That matters because the same IOR material is sold as paywalled transcripts elsewhere: verified 2026-10-09 by recovering a bride's name and marriage date, from two independent FIBIS indexes, for a 1846 Bombay marriage a family archive had been unable to read behind a paid trial. It also indexes Allen's Indian Mail, the Bombay Times, the Times of India and the Gentleman's Magazine announcements, which carry people home again — one officer's death in north Wales in 1862 is recorded there because the Anglo-Indian press reported it.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive, 2026-10-10. TWO WARNINGS, BOTH MEASURED. (1) THE DEFAULT SEARCH IS SOUNDEX AND ITS RESULT COUNT IS NOT A FINDING COUNT. A default search for the surname D'Arcy returned twelve sources; TEN WERE NOT D'ARCY — the soundex matches TRACY, TRACEY, TRAISE, DRUCE and D'ROSE, so a «Gentleman's Magazine death announcement for Robert D'Arcy» turned out to be Robert Alexander Druce. Open the rows before quoting a number; «Exact matches only» is in the advanced panel and gave 29 sources for the same surname. (2) SUBMITTING THE SEARCH FORM PROGRAMMATICALLY RETURNS «Sorry, invalid search please try again. Please do not remotely search this site using a bot or external program.» Filling the fields and clicking the button works normally. Treat the site as one to read at human pace, and do not script its forms.

providers.name: Ancestor.co.za
providers.what: A South African commercial document-retrieval service. It takes a request for a named estate or death notice, retrieves it from the archives and uploads a scan to the requester's account on its own site. Observed charging 70 ZAR per death notice in December 2023, with a stated turnaround of up to 21 days, and notifying by email on upload. It is a RETRIEVAL AGENT rather than an index: there is no public catalogue to search, so it answers a reference you already have and cannot tell you whether one exists. Added from the Booyzen archive, which found two of its own death notices delivered this way in January 2024 and never ingested.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Booyzen archive on a first-hand transaction record, not a survey. ACCESS CLASS STILL NEEDS A PERSON: what an ordinary visitor pays, and whether an account is required to request at all, were not verified - the evidence is one family's receipts, and having used a site is not a survey.

providers.name: Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin
providers.what: The Berlin central and regional library's digital collections, and for genealogy the thing that matters is THE BERLINER ADRESSBUCH, 1799 to 1943, complete, free, no account. A Berlin address book gives a householder's FORENAME, TRADE, POSTAL DISTRICT, STREET AND HOUSE NUMBER, year by year, so a household can be followed between censuses and a trade watched as it changes — which in the Berlin volumes of 1938 to 1943 is not a metaphor. Three sections per volume: the Namenteil (by surname), the Straßenteil (by street, listing a house's owner, manager and every tenant), and a trades section. THE POST-WAR BOOKS ARE HERE UNDER DIFFERENT IDENTIFIERS and are set in Antiqua, so their text layer simply works; the pre-1944 books are FRAKTUR and theirs does not. HOW TO USE IT WITHOUT AN ACCOUNT: a Solr query endpoint at /viewer/api/v1/index/query takes FULLTEXT: and PI_TOPSTRUCT: and returns page order numbers; /viewer/api/v1/records/<PI>/pages/<order>/text/ returns a page's OCR as IIIF annotations; and /viewer/content/<PI>/<width>/0/<8-digit>.jpg returns the page image at any width. The ALTO XML endpoint is permission-controlled and returns 403 for these volumes, so word coordinates are not available and a run must be found by cropping. FOUR THINGS MEASURED IN USE, ALL OF THEM ABOUT THE FRAKTUR TEXT LAYER. (1) SEARCHING FOR A RARE SURNAME IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT: the headword is routinely mangled past matching, and in one volume a street name came out as “Diessenbachsir”, so the year was found only by reading the run in place. (2) DIGITS ARE WORSE THAN LETTERS: a Fraktur 5 read as 6 and a 4 read as 1 were both caught only at the image, and a house number taken from the text layer should not be trusted. (3) THE LONG S is rendered as f or j, which is a help as well as a hindrance — it proves a street name that no spelling without an s could produce. (4) THE PER-PAGE OCR CAN INTERLEAVE TWO ADJACENT COLUMNS LINE BY LINE WITHOUT SAYING SO, silently attributing one surname's entries to its neighbour; the pages are four columns wide, a run can split across a column break with the headword repeated at the top of the next one, and an alphabetical check at the image is the only way to catch either. *** AND THE HOLDING IS SPLIT ACROSS FOUR RECORD IDENTIFIERS WITH A SIX-YEAR HOLE IN IT, WHICH IS THE FIRST THING TO KNOW: *** PI 34115495 is the Berliner Adreßbuch for 1903 TO 1943 and nothing earlier; PI 34115512 is the SAME TITLE for 1873 TO 1896; 1897 TO 1902 ARE NOT DIGITISED UNDER EITHER and return zero pages; PI 34117222 holds the post-war Namenteil and Branchen volumes of 1955 to 1970; and PI 15849358 the telephone books of 1970 to 1980. A query against the wrong anchor returns ZERO AND LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE AN ABSENT SURNAME, so run a common-surname control (Schmidt returns four figures a volume) before believing any zero. ONE MORE THING ABOUT THE PRE-1900 VOLUMES: THEY PRINT FORENAME INITIALS ONLY — “A., Beamter”, “O., Lederhändler”, “J., Ww.” — and a single letter is the worst-OCR'd thing on a Fraktur page, so a negative on a FORENAME cannot be drawn from them at all. Full forenames begin with the 1903 volume. *** AND THE RULE THAT TURNS A BERLIN ADDRESS INTO A REGISTRY OFFICE, MEASURED ON TWO HOUSES IN TWO INDEPENDENT SUBURBS. *** For a street in a suburb that ran its own administration, THE BERLIN STREET DIRECTORY GIVES THE COURT AND NOT THE STANDESAMT — "W. 62 Lutherstr. · A.G. Charlottb. — L.G. III. (geh. z. Charlottenburg)" — because the suburb kept its own offices. The answer is in the suburb's own part of the volume and it takes two pages: one list defines each Standesamt BY STADTBEZIRK, and a second maps every STREET AND HOUSE-NUMBER RANGE to a Bezirk. IN CHARLOTTENBURG A STREET NAME IS NOT AN ADDRESS — the HOUSE NUMBER selects the Bezirk, and the same street is split across several. Lutherstr. 12-43 is one Bezirk and the rest of the street is not; Joachimsthalerstr. runs 1-4, 5-9 and 10-21 across three. A reading that names the street without the number has not finished. AND THE TWO VOLUMES DIFFER IN WHAT THEY WILL ANSWER: the 1913 volume defines the offices by Stadtbezirk ("Standesamt I. Rankestr. 10. Umfassend die Stadtbezirke Hochschulviertel 1-7, Am Kurfürstendamm 1-6, Ostviertel 1-8"), while THE 1903 VOLUME NAMES ITS OFFICES AND THEIR REGISTRARS AND NOT THEIR DISTRICTS AT ALL — so a 1903 address can be resolved to a Bezirk but NOT from that volume alone to an office. CHARLOTTENBURG HAD TWO REGISTRY OFFICES IN 1903 (Rankestr. 10 and Kirchstr. 10) AND THREE BY 1913, so a mapping read off one year must not be carried to the other. Finally the numerals are the first thing the Fraktur OCR loses: a range printed 5-9 came through as "5 -'i" and a house number 34 as 31, so the figure that decides the office is exactly the figure that must be read at the image.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Luwinski family archive, which has worked the Berliner Adressbuch volumes of 1925-1943 and 1955-1980 over three weeks. The access class IS surveyed: the images and the OCR endpoints were used repeatedly with no account and no fee.

providers.name: Open Archieven
providers.what: The open index behind more than two hundred Dutch and Belgian archives — civil registration, population registers, church books and memorial cards, pooled and searchable by name, with an open API. It tells you the entry exists and which shelf it is on; the scan, where there is one, is the holding archive's to show. Distinct from WieWasWie, which is the official portal over much of the same material.
providers.surveyNote: Their own Spelregels: the API is free, a few parts want a key, no more than four requests a second, send a recognisable program name, and name the holding archive as the source.

providers.name: IdentityNumber.org
providers.what: Transcribed South African death notices, with older marriage and baptism records, immigration records and British concentration camp records alongside them. A free tier exists behind a sign-up and the fuller tiers are paid, which is why this is filed mixed rather than paid. NOTE WHAT ELSE IT IS: the same site sells identity verification on LIVING people, and its upper tiers list home addresses and phone numbers. This atlas indexes where historical records are held and points at the record collections only; the people-search half is named here so nobody mistakes the listing for an endorsement of it.

providers.name: OldNews.com
providers.what: Digitised historical newspapers, indexed by town. The CATALOGUE is harvested and published here — 38,151 papers in 6,450 towns across 75 countries, of which 5,968 towns join to a point on this map — because their robots.txt says Allow: /en/newspapers/* and the whole structure is in the URL. WHAT IT COSTS IS NOT KNOWN, and that is why this says unsurveyed rather than free or paid: the same robots.txt disallows /*/record and /*/search, so the pages that would answer it are the pages not to read. There is a log-in; whether an image is free behind it has not been established, and a colour on the map is a promise this cannot keep yet.

providers.name: SANDF Documentation Centre (Department of Defence Archives), Pretoria
providers.what: Holds the personnel files of former Union Defence Force, South African Defence Force and SANDF members, indexed by service number, identity number or date of birth, place of birth, unit and dates of service. A copy is requested in writing (Private Bag X289, Pretoria 0001); it does not send records electronically, so a postal or fax address must be in the request, and a copy of an identity document is asked for. Used by the Lerena archive on 16 October 2026: an email request for a grandfather's file, sent to an address that no current official page confirms (archive@dod.mil.za); no reply yet. Fees and the consent a descendant needs were not verified. The Department of Defence's own website (www.dod.mil.za) did not respond when tried on 16 October 2026, from this machine, over either http or https; the address is the department's published one, not a verified live page.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Lerena archive. Access class still needs a person: fee and next-of-kin consent rules are unverified.

providers.name: The SAAF Forum (an unofficial South African Air Force website and forum)
providers.what: An unofficial enthusiast site (its footer says so) with a forum, open to read and needing an account to post. A sticky thread in 'The SAAF!' points to the UK National Archives' AIR 54 squadron operations record books. Its contact page lists how to request a personnel record from the SANDF Documentation Centre and four private military researchers. Read by the Lerena archive on 16 October 2026; a post asking how to find a man in 12 Squadron is drafted and not yet made.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Lerena archive. Unofficial; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: FreeCEN — UK census transcriptions
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of the UK censuses, free and with NO ACCOUNT for searching (the search page is /search_queries/new). Pick a census year from 1841 to 1911, a county by Chapman code and a surname and optional first name, and the results come back as a list that opens to the whole household, with relationship, marital status, age, occupation and birthplace for each member and the piece, enumeration district, folio, page and schedule. That makes it the free way to see a household and a lodger beside a head, which an index to one person cannot. COVERAGE IS PER COUNTY AND PER YEAR AND UNEVEN. For Hertfordshire the 1851 census was found (the Baldock district, Weston among its parishes); searches of Hertfordshire for 1841 and for 1861 returned nothing, which is not a finding that the records do not exist. A control surname at the same county and year should be run before a nil result is quoted. Birthplace is the parish as the enumerator heard it, and ages are often a year or two out against a baptism.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Luwinski archive. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Hertfordshire Names Online — Hertfordshire Archives and Local Studies
providers.what: A free, account-free name index to the Hertfordshire archive's holdings: marriages and marriage licences (1538 to 1925), wills (1413 to 1857, from the archdeaconries of Huntingdon (Hitchin Division) and St Albans), the poor (1623 to 1915), apprentices, crime and punishment, non-conformist registers, newspapers and tithe records. One search by exact surname, an optional keyword (a parish name works) and a year range returns a count per index, and each opens to a table. It gives what is INDEXED and not the document: a will or a licence bond is a reference number, and a copy is £11.45 an item, viewable free at Hertfordshire Archives. It is the second index to cross-check a FreeREG marriage, and it is where a yeoman's will before 1858 turns up, which a register will not show. Spell the surname both ways; the licence in the example was indexed under Phillips and the register entry under Philips.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Luwinski archive. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Macoupin County ILGenWeb — cemetery burial listings
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of burials in Macoupin County, Illinois cemeteries, one page per letter-range (Calvary, Mt. Olive: calvarya.html, calvaryc.html … calvaryt.html), each row linking to a photograph of the stone. Free, no account. Read 17 October 2026 for the Calvary Catholic cemetery at Mount Olive: the R–S page lists thirteen Spudic/Spudick burials with birth and death years and photographs. It is a transcription by volunteers, not a register: the years come from the stones, not from a death record, and the page does not say how complete the cemetery coverage is.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Spudic/Polovich family page (External-Family-Work/spudic-polovich). Licence not stated on the pages read.

providers.name: UK Genealogy Archives
providers.what: A family-run British site, online since 1998 and free to view, that hosts its own searchable transcripts rather than pointing elsewhere. What its collections page lists as searchable: the England & Wales censuses of 1841, 1851, 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901 and 1911; marriage registers for Anglesey, Berkshire, Brecknock, Devon, Dorset, Durham, Gloucestershire, Hampshire, Leicestershire, Middlesex, Norfolk, Northumberland, Shropshire, Surrey and Wiltshire; baptism and burial registers for Devon, Dorset, Durham and Northumberland; the Phillimore marriage volumes (over 600 parishes and about 248,000 marriages, the site says) and a set of parish registers (over 40, with free images of the original pages where it has them); an England & Wales marriages 1538–1921 transcript; the First World War medals and awards; the 1873 Return of Owners of Land; the Samuel Lewis topographical dictionaries; trade directories and gazetteers; Who Was Who 1897–1916; school, college and university registers; and the peerage and pedigree books: Burke's Peerage and Landed Gentry, Debrett's, Dod's 1841 and the Heralds' Visitations. WHAT IT IS NOT: mostly transcripts, so the ordinary experience is an index with no image; only the parish-register collection says it carries page images. The county series cover parishes the site chose and carry the date ranges it states (some run 1538 to 1837, some to 1920 or 1950), so a name missing from one is not shown absent from the parish. The site also has sections for Scotland, Ireland, Wales, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands, but the searchable collections above are almost all England and Wales. Every figure here is the site's own statement from its home and collections pages; none has been measured against a known entry. Pages carry advertising and affiliate links to commercial genealogy services, which it discloses in a banner.
providers.triageNote: Added 2 November 2026 at David's request, from the site's own home page and collections list (https://ukga.org/browse.php), read in the browser. The server answered an automated fetch of /search.php with HTTP 429, which was left alone; nothing here comes from a search. Not yet measured: run a control surname in a parish the site lists before quoting any nil from it.

providers.name: Javna ustanova Spomen-područje Jasenovac — poimenični popis žrtava KL Jasenovac 1941.–1945.
providers.what: The Jasenovac Memorial Site's own name-by-name list of victims of the Jasenovac camp complex, 1941–1945, searchable on its website (page «Pregled i pretraga poimeničnog popisa žrtava KL Jasenovac 1941.-1945.»). Search fields: surname, first name, municipality of birth, place of birth, year of birth and camp (Jasenovac, Stara Gradiška); each result shows father's first name, birth year, municipality and place of birth, nationality, manner of death, who caused it, year and place of death, camp and execution site. The page states no login. A separate form on the site requests a printout of the data. It is the Memorial Site's list, not the Belgrade Museum of Genocide Victims' register (see muzej-genocida): the two are compiled separately and are best searched both. The institution's annual reports give 83,747 names in 2016 and say the list is still being added to; the page itself states no total. Read from the site on 2026-11-04; what an ordinary visitor pays and how the list is paged was not checked. Interface in Croatian.
providers.triageNote: Home page and victim-list search page read on 2026-11-04. Wikidata Q16087601 is the item labelled «Jasenovac Memorial Site»; whether it is the institution or the site was not checked. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Holocaust Survivors and Victims Names Database — United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
providers.what: The US Holocaust Memorial Museum's names database: a name record for each person who appears in a document in its collections, its Survivors' Registry and records from other organisations (census records, registration forms, ghetto and camp lists, death lists). Covers Jews, Roma and Sinti, Poles and other Slavic peoples, Soviet prisoners of war and political prisoners. Two searches: Names (last and first name, each Exact with wildcards, Fuzzy, or D-M Soundex for Eastern European and Yiddish variants) and Lists and Sources (title, author, year, place, provenance, keywords). The page says some resources are not online and that the full database can be used in the Museum's reading room. Its record total and whether an account is needed were not stated on the page. Read on 2026-11-04.
providers.triageNote: Database page read on 2026-11-04. Access class and record count still need a person.

providers.name: Archives of the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum
providers.what: Original camp records of Auschwitz, spring 1940 to January 1945: records of the six camp chancellery departments (commandant's orders, prisoner personal files, death certificates, daily prisoner count books, camp hospital record books), censored prisoner letters and postcards, SS Hygiene Institute and Central Construction Board records, resistance materials including illegally compiled lists of deceased women prisoners, and trial records (mostly copies). Also copies of transport lists of Jews deported from Drancy, Westerbork, Theresienstadt and Berlin, mostly copies of prisoner transfer lists for other camps (original Mauthausen prisoner file cards are held), records of about a dozen sub-camps (fullest for Jawischowitz and Janinagrube), the postwar Bellert hospital book and lists of liberated prisoners by nationality. For Soviet prisoners of war: 7,646 camp record sheets (scanned, with a 1990s database of 7,646 personal records) and a 470-page book of deceased Soviet POWs (database of 8,333 personal records; documents at least 8,320 deaths from 7 October 1941 to 28 February 1942). Does not hold a full set of Jewish deportee registrations. The collection page describes no online search tool and no request procedure; its Contact page is linked but the office for archive requests is not named.
providers.triageNote: Collection overview and the Soviet POW data page were read. No search form or request route was seen; a person must find out from the Museum how to ask for a named prisoner, and whether the 'Central Register of Prisoners' database is public.

providers.name: USHMM - Primary Source Databases (list of electronic resources)
providers.what: A curated list of 39 databases and archives about the Holocaust and Nazi-era persecution, grouped as Camps, First-Person Accounts, Life Under the Nazi Regime, Propaganda, Refugees, Resistance, United States, War Crime Trials and Additional Resources. Name-bearing entries include Arolsen Archives, Kazerne Dossin deportation lists and victim photographs, the Fortunoff and USC Shoah Foundation testimony archives, JDC Archives, DigiBaeck (Leo Baeck Institute), a Nuremberg-laws index of Jews stripped of German nationality, 'The Jewish Question: Documents from the BDC' (Gale), Shanghai Municipal Police files on individual Jewish refugees (Gale) and the Dachau trials records (Gale). Most entries are intended for use inside the Museum; only some are marked as available to researchers outside it, and most carry no access note. It is a pointer list, not a name search.
providers.triageNote: The full list was read. Many items are Gale or Adam Matthew subscription products hosted for Museum visitors; what a home user pays or needs was not seen. Useful as a map of further sources.

providers.name: Gedenkbuch - Opfer der Verfolgung der Juden unter der nationalsozialistischen Gewaltherrschaft in Deutschland 1933-1945 (Bundesarchiv)
providers.what: Searchable memorial database of Jewish victims of persecution in Germany 1933-1945, run by the Bundesarchiv. A single name field (first name, surname or birth name; terms combined with AND; case and accent insensitive; * and ? wildcards) or an advanced search by places (birth, residence, deportation) and dates (birth, deportation, emigration). Results are 10 per page, sorted alphabetically by surname and exportable as CSV. German with an English interface. Lists victims of the persecution of Jews in the German territory of 1933-1945 only; does not claim to cover non-Jewish victims. The page does not say whether it is free of charge or how many names it holds.
providers.triageNote: Search page was read. Entry counts and cost are not stated. The Atlas already has a 'bundesarchiv' row for the main site; this is the separate apps.bundesarchiv.de service.

providers.name: Digitaal Joods Monument (Jewish Cultural Quarter)
providers.what: Online monument with an individual page for each Dutch Jew, Roma or Sinto (and those who fled to the Netherlands) who was persecuted and did not survive the Holocaust; described as covering more than 109,000 people. A name is added when the death is certain. Maintained by the Jewish Cultural Quarter, Amsterdam; English and Dutch versions; a search page and a login/sign-up option exist, and visitors can contribute (User contributions). Related sources it describes: the 'In Memoriam' book of 101,414 Jews deported from the Netherlands with no known grave, and the National Database of Victims of Persecution (NDVS), run by the Jewish Museum and the Westerbork Camp Memorial Center. The pages read do not say what a free visit includes or what the login adds.
providers.triageNote: Home page and a search-engine summary of its about/FAQ pages were read; the about and FAQ pages themselves returned only navigation. Per-person fields and costs still need a person to check.

providers.name: Oorlogsgravenstichting (Dutch War Graves Foundation)
providers.what: Dutch foundation, active since 1946, that has registered about 180,000 people in the Netherlands as war victims (including those who died in the Second World War and in later conflicts) and maintains about 50,000 Dutch war graves worldwide. Collects and shares victims' life stories. The site has a search box for a person, location or story and a separate exact-search page. The home page read is in Dutch; no English version was seen.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Search fields and what a person record shows were not seen; whether it includes camp deaths of Dutch victims abroad needs a person to test.

providers.name: Dokumentationsarchiv des oesterreichischen Widerstandes (DOeW) - Opfersuche
providers.what: Austrian resistance and persecution research archive (research archive, library, photo archive) with an online victim search covering Austrian Shoah victims, Spiegelgrund victims, deaths from political persecution 1938-1945, and men and women registered by the Gestapo Wien (some of whom survived). The site states a total of 78,743 entries and says the databases are a work in progress. Basic search by first and last name (umlauts and the eszett match alternative spellings); extended search by residence, birth date, birthplace with a phonetic option; wildcards * and ?. Does not claim to list every Austrian victim.
providers.triageNote: Home page and search help text read. Direct URL of the search form was not captured, so deepLink is null. Cost not stated.

providers.name: KZ-Gedenkstaette Dachau - Archive, Digital Memorial Book and prisoner information requests
providers.what: Memorial site archive with a Digital Memorial Book, 'The Victims of the Dachau Concentration Camp 1933-1945' (people who died in Dachau, its satellite camps and on the death marches, to 31 July 1945; the memorial estimates about 41,500 murdered, many nameless, and the book does not include those who died in other camps or on transports between them). Linked at gedenkbuch.kz-gedenkstaette-dachau.de/en. Information on individual prisoners is requested through an online form that asks for the requester's relationship to the person and any known birth data; the form gives no response time, fee or eligibility rule. Also lists an audio and video archive and a library.
providers.triageNote: Research menu, Digital Memorial Book page and request form were read; the Memorial Book search itself was not opened.

providers.name: Buchenwald Memorial - Online Books of the Dead
providers.what: Two online books of the dead for research on people who died at Buchenwald: a book for the concentration camp 1937-1945 (more than 56,000 dead; excludes people deported from Buchenwald who died in other camps) at totenbuch.buchenwald.de, and a database of more than 7,000 names for Soviet Special Camp No. 2 (1945-1950), based on the camp's death registers and camp journal, at totenbuch-speziallager.buchenwald.de/recherche/. The memorial site also lists an online photo archive, collections and a library. The page gives no search fields; the English site names no general archive-request route other than a contacts page.
providers.triageNote: Online Books of the Dead page was read; the book sites themselves were not opened. Contact emails for each book are on the page.

providers.name: Mauthausen Memorial - Collections database, Memorial Book and person searches
providers.what: Memorial's person-search guidance recommends starting with the Arolsen Archives online database, then sending a research request by web form with as much information as possible on the person (open to relatives, people asking about a specific person, and researchers on SS personnel). A central collections database at collections.mauthausen-memorial.org (documents, photographs, oral history, artefacts, library) is online without registration since January 2026; the page does not say whether it can be searched by name. For people who died at Mauthausen and its satellite camps, an online Memorial Book for the Dead is at raumdernamen.mauthausen-memorial.org. A page of fees for use of the collections exists; the amounts were not seen.
providers.triageNote: Searching-for-persons and collection-databases pages read. Fees, and whether the collections database searches names, are not stated.

providers.name: Stutthof Museum in Sztutowo - Archives and searching for former prisoners
providers.what: Museum archive that issues official certificates of a person's stay in the camp, to former prisoners, their families, and Polish and foreign institutions. Records are only partly preserved; the museum has identified about 75% of prisoners by name. An online search covers only a fragment of the list (fields: surname, first name, camp number, date and place of birth, place of residence, occupation); scans exist only for record-book documents with reference numbers starting I-IIE-. A request uses an 'Investigation card' PDF sent to poszukiwania@stutthof.org or by post, giving the person's name, surname and date of birth. The museum sent 36,767 names of Polish prisoners to the straty.pl victims database.
providers.triageNote: Search-for-prisoners page read. The online search form was not opened; fee for certificates not stated.

providers.name: KZ-Gedenkstaette Neuengamme - Archive and Death Register 1940-1945
providers.what: Archive of the Neuengamme concentration camp and its satellite camps, also resistance and persecution in Northern Germany and Hamburg under the Nazis. Holds documents, photographs, plans, drawings, audio and visual media and objects, including death registers and infirmary laboratory records hidden by prisoners in April 1945, personal documents, survivor testimonies and interviews. Answers relatives' requests about a prisoner's fate through an online archive request form, compiling information from several archives into a person-related database. An online Death Register 1940-1945 is listed. Use of the collection needs a written request explaining the research project and an appointment (Monday to Friday, 9-17). Does not offer open walk-in access to the collection.
providers.triageNote: Archive page read. The death register page itself was only seen in a search listing, not opened; its search fields and counts are unverified.

providers.name: Terezin Initiative Institute - holocaust.cz (victims and documents databases)
providers.what: Czech Holocaust documentation site of the Terezin Initiative Institute, in Czech, English and German. Its home page links a victims database (entries with birth date, places such as Terezin, Treblinka or Auschwitz, and a status of died), a document database of scans such as passport applications, identity-card applications and inquiries about a person, a Terezin ghetto section, a section on the persecution and genocide of Roma and Sinti in the Czech lands, and survivor testimonies. The home page text states no counts and no search instructions.
providers.triageNote: Home page only; the victims and document database URLs were not captured, so deepLink is null. A person should confirm search fields and counts.

providers.name: IPN - Straty osobowe i ofiary represji pod okupacja niemiecka 1939-1945 (straty.pl)
providers.what: Institute of National Remembrance documentation programme building a named list of citizens of the Second Polish Republic who were repressed or killed under German occupation: soldiers, prisoners of war, prisoners of camps and prisons, and Holocaust victims. Entries carry personal data, the type, cause and circumstances of repression, the source and descriptive notes such as biographies. Search by person name or by place and type of repression; a questionnaire lets relatives report information. States 5,565,892 victims and repressed persons in total, 5,059,663 known by name and 506,229 anonymous. Polish-language page; whether other languages and any cost exist is not stated.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; it does not name straty.pl but the domain was fetched directly and the Stutthof museum links to it. Counts are the page's own figures and cover the whole programme, not only Jewish victims.

providers.name: OBD Memorial - united databank of Soviet war losses (Russian Ministry of Defence)
providers.what: United databank on defenders of the Fatherland reported dead or missing in the Great Patriotic War and afterwards: records of persons, burials and documents on irrecoverable losses. Source areas include reports on irrecoverable losses, hospital and medical battalion documents, casualty updates, burial name lists, prisoner-of-war documents, de-listing orders, card indices, and digital and printed Memory Books. Fields searched include surname, first name, patronymic, year and place of birth, rank, last place of service. Quick Search is Russian only; Advanced Search adds source choice and extra areas for authorised users; a tab finds soldiers by reconsignment points when the unit is unknown. Not the same organisation as the human-rights group Memorial. Soviet POW material includes records that matter for POWs held in German camps.
providers.triageNote: The English help page was read; the main info page returned an error to the fetcher and the search interface was not opened. A person should test it, and confirm whether an account is needed beyond 'authorised users'.

providers.name: Mosaic of Victims - Hungarian Roma in the Second World War (National Archives of Hungary)
providers.what: Online resource of the National Archives of Hungary, made under an IHRA grant, with three databases of Roma victims: Roma deported from Hungary in 1944-1945 to Dachau, Buchenwald, Bergen-Belsen, Mauthausen, Natzweiler, Ravensbruck and subcamps (1,470 deported persons as of February 2023, with more still being identified); Hungarian Roma soldiers and civilian victims 1939-1945; and victims of ten mass executions between September 1944 and March 1945. Identifications relied on surnames, mothers' surnames, traditional Roma occupations and places of residence assessed case by case, and the page warns that not every person labelled Roma in camp records was Roma. The databases are hosted on the Archives' online portal; no search instructions were given on the page read.
providers.triageNote: Page read. The portal and search form were not opened; no count for the soldiers and civilians database.

providers.name: Kazerne Dossin - Memorial, Museum and Documentation Centre on Holocaust and Human Rights
providers.what: Belgian memorial at the former Dossin barracks, from which 25,490 Jews and 353 Roma were deported on 28 transports between 1942 and 1944, mostly to Auschwitz-Birkenau. The home page offers an online archive and a reading room for research and for questions about a family member's experience, and a contact page. An image bank at beeldbank.kazernedossin.eu is described by the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum as holding original documents on the Holocaust in Belgium (official records, personal documents, memoirs, oral histories), with deportation lists and victim photographs openly accessible and other collections needing a visit and registration for unaffiliated researchers. The image bank site itself loaded only a 'Loading Application' screen.
providers.triageNote: Main site read; the image bank description is second-hand from USHMM's list and its own page did not render. Needs a person to confirm what is searchable by name.

providers.name: Fortunoff Video Archive for Holocaust Testimonies (Yale University Library)
providers.what: Archive of over 4,400 testimonies of Holocaust survivors, witnesses and liberators. Searchable remotely through the Aviary platform (instructions on registering in Aviary are on the archive's site), with a Visual Search tool and a Publication Database of texts that cite testimony. Also available at access sites worldwide (generally universities, museums and memorials). Quoting testimony in publications needs permission; using video or audio excerpts in films or podcasts needs a licence. The page does not state what an individual Aviary account costs or who is eligible.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Interview-level search by name or place was not tried.

providers.name: DigiBaeck - Leo Baeck Institute digital collections
providers.what: Digital collections of the Leo Baeck Institute documenting German-speaking Jewry in the modern era: personal documents, correspondence, family and community histories, genealogical materials and business records; about 5,000 memoirs and manuscripts; over 5,000 art items and objects; over 25,000 photographs; over 1,600 rare books and over 200 periodicals fully online; interviews including over 1,000 Austrian Heritage Collection interviews and oral histories with 253 German-Jewish refugees. Searched by a keyword box or browse links; only digitised items are returned. The site is available in English and German. The page does not state whether access is free or whether a surname search of family collections is supported.
providers.triageNote: Landing page read. Not a 1941-45 source as such; useful for emigre families from Germany, Austria and Bohemia.

providers.name: ICRC Archives - Central Agency tracing files, Second World War
providers.what: The International Committee of the Red Cross holds data on individuals collected by it and its tracing agencies in conflicts since 1870, to restore family links and protect prisoners of war, civilian internees and war victims: card files, lists, individual files and general documents. Documents become public after 70 years under conditions set out in a linked PDF. A search-engine summary of other ICRC pages reports the Agency's card index passed 36 million cards by June 1947 and that new research requests are currently paused with a notice pointing to tracing.archives@icrc.org; that status was not confirmed on the page read. Individuals are found through nominal lists plus birth date and place, father's first name and POW number.
providers.triageNote: Access page read; request process and current status are not on it. The pause notice came from a search snippet and must be checked at icrc.org before anyone submits a request.

providers.name: Memorial de la Shoah (Paris) - Documentation Centre
providers.what: Paris memorial with a documentation centre made up of archives, a photo library, a library and audiovisual collections, plus archives of its temporary exhibitions. An online documentation portal is described as searching for people, documents, photos, films, books and posters, and a form lets visitors request information about a person. Entry to the memorial is free with no reservation. The page read states no holdings counts and does not mention a list of names of people deported from France.
providers.triageNote: English home page read; the portal and request form were not opened. Needs a person to confirm what the portal holds for named deportees.

providers.name: Commonwealth War Graves Commission
providers.what: The Commission founded by Royal Charter in 1917 on behalf of the governments of Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, South Africa and the United Kingdom. Its site states a database of 1.7 million men and women of the Commonwealth who died in the two world wars, searched through a War Dead search box, with separate searches for cemeteries and memorials and an archive of over 60,000 items (correspondence, maintenance and tour reports, staff records, photographs, press cuttings). For the Second World War the roll also includes Commonwealth civilians who died between 3 September 1939 and 31 December 1947 through enemy action, Allied weapons of war or in an enemy prison camp (the Civilian War Dead 1939-1945, whose roll is held at Westminster Abbey); the Find War Dead search reaches them under its Served In menu. It does not hold German, Soviet, Polish or other non-Commonwealth dead, and service records themselves are held by national archives, not by the Commission.
providers.triageNote: About us and Find records pages and a search summary of the Find War Dead page read; the Find War Dead page itself returned 403 to the fetch, so fields and any charge are unconfirmed. A person must run the search and say what it costs.
