providers.triageNote: Opened the Western Cape Government archives page (address, hours, family-history guide links) and the Edinburgh 'Whites Writing Whiteness' page for the repository (series list, access rules) on 2026-11-08. Did not open the PDF guides; the series list is from the third-party directory, not the archive's own page.

providers.name: Cape Slave Transactions (Stamouers / eGGSA)
providers.what: An index page on the Stamouers site (part of eGGSA) that links three compilations about slaves at the Cape under the VOC: a database built on a standard printed work on slaves and free blacks at the Cape for 1658 to 1700, a database of sale deeds for 1658 to 1731 abstracted from a professor's research, and a transcription of the 1714 VOC Slave Lodge census. The first is offered as a PDF of about half a megabyte. The page asks for corrections with documented proof and for acknowledgement of the author and eGGSA when the material is reused. It does not describe fields or whether the files can be searched by name, and I did not open the linked files.
providers.triageNote: Opened the index page on 2026-11-08; did not open the linked databases. Host stamouers.com already has a row for its main site; this is a distinct page.

providers.name: Slavery at the Cape (Iziko Museums of South Africa)
providers.what: A web project by Iziko Museums about the enslaved society of the Cape Colony from the 1650s to emancipation in 1834, with the focus on slavery within Africa rather than the transatlantic trade. Sections cover the VOC, slave routes, private lives, resistance and legacy, the Slave Lodge building and its inhabitants and administration, and the Groot Constantia estate, which includes a register of slaves. A Resources section lists primary documents, a bibliography and personal histories. The page I read only links to the historical-sources section, so I do not know whether it gives lists of names; I did not open those sub-pages.

at.place: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read its section list; did not open the Resources, historical-sources or Groot Constantia register pages.

providers.name: UCT Libraries Special Collections online archive catalogue (AtoM)
providers.what: The University of Cape Town Libraries' archival catalogue, built on AtoM, with global and advanced search and browse lists by subject, place and date. The one page I opened is the subject term 'Slavery--Cape Colony', which points to a single fonds, 'Slavery Miscellany', created by the Cape Town Slave Registry Office. It contains deeds of slave sales, mortgage bonds that used enslaved people as security, an extract from the Registry's register and other papers about enslaved people and indentured apprentices, dated roughly 1821 to 1834. I did not browse the catalogue's other collections.
providers.triageNote: Opened the subject-term page on 2026-11-08 only; the rest of the catalogue and whether the fonds is digitised were not checked.

providers.name: British Concentration Camps of the South African War 1900-1902 (UCT database)
providers.what: A University of Cape Town research database built from the camp registers of the camps the British army set up for residents of the Transvaal and Orange Free State in the South African War. The site lists 45 camps with history pages (17 in the Transvaal, 10 in the Free State, 9 in Natal, 9 in the Cape Colony) and offers browse and search of persons, camps and farms, and a unique-ID search. It covers 1900 to 1902 and usually leaves out returning prisoners of war and movements after 31 May 1902. The page warns that the project is ongoing, some registers are incomplete and the data contains duplicates and variants. The page shows a Login section but does not say who may use the data; I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the database home page on 2026-11-08 and read its coverage and caveats; did not search or log in, so access terms are unknown.

providers.name: South African Jewish Rootsbank (Kaplan Centre, University of Cape Town)
providers.what: The South African Jewish Database, part of the Jewish Migration and Genealogy Project at the Isaac and Jessie Kaplan Centre, UCT, aiming to document about 15,000 core families who came to Southern Africa between 1850 and 1950 from Britain, Germany, Lithuania, Latvia and Belarus. Search categories include the Poor Jew's Temporary Shelter database, births, deaths and estates, marriages, cemeteries, communities and congregations, military records, naturalisations, societies, passenger arrivals and shipping manifests. The page says the Kaplan Centre holds passenger arrivals registers for 1924 to 1929 and manifest copies for 1890 to 1930 but no personal certificates, and that scan requests were delayed during Covid. Each category has its own search page; I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open individual search pages. The Covid notice suggests the page text is dated. A row exists for the JewishGen Southern Africa SIG, which is a different site.

providers.name: Huguenot Memorial Museum, Franschhoek
providers.what: The museum of the Huguenot Society of South Africa at Lambrechts Street, Franschhoek, housed in a reconstruction of an 18th-century manor house. Its six display rooms tell the story of the Huguenots as refugees and as settlers at the Cape, and the Flight exhibit has a list of Huguenots who arrived at the Cape with signatures from archival documents beside some names. The Family exhibit and annex show family ties and household possessions. The page gives a virtual tour and contact details but no opening hours, and it does not mention a genealogy service or library; I did not look for one elsewhere on the site.
providers.triageNote: Opened the museum page on 2026-11-08. The existing row for the Huguenot Society covers the society's own page; this row is the museum. Wikidata Q2429656 matched by name and description (museum in South Africa).

providers.name: Africana Library, Kimberley
providers.what: A research library in Kimberley, Northern Cape, specialising in the history of the Diamond Fields. The page lists about 14,000 books, 640 manuscripts and 12,000 photographs, early books in Tswana, San, Zulu and Xhosa, Anglo-Boer War material, and local newspapers from 1870 to the present. It mentions directories and voters' lists but does not call them genealogy sources. The building opened as a public library in 1887, was restored as an Africana Library in 1986 and became a national monument in 1990. The page advises phoning a week or more ahead; I did not see a catalogue address.
providers.triageNote: Opened the library page on 2026-11-08. Holdings figures and the newspaper range are as stated there; no catalogue or finding aid was opened.

providers.name: British 1820 Settlers to South Africa (1820settlers.com genealogy database)
providers.what: A free genealogy site on the British settlers of 1820, their descendants and researchers, built on TNG software. The home page lists settler surnames, settler parties, ships, letters and farm records, with media for photos, certificates, census returns, probate notices and maps, and transcriptions of Anglican and Methodist baptisms and marriages, Cape civil death indices, burials and Cape movement permits. Search is by first and last name, with advanced, family and site searches. The page says no registration is needed to view data and that, as of 15 August 2025, the project is closed and no records will be added or updated. The page does not give a record count.
providers.triageNote: Opened the genealogy home page on 2026-11-08; the site root is a frameset wrapper. Did not run a search. Note the maintainer says the site is closed to updates.

providers.name: Basler Afrika Bibliographien (research library and archive for Southern Africa, Namibia focus)
providers.what: A research library and documentation centre in Basel for Southern Africa, with a focus on Namibia. The home page shows a library and an archive, each with its own catalogue, and a meta-catalogue (PARC) for Africana collections in Basel and Frankfurt. It publishes works by Southern African authors, with a growing open-access list, and the page says it has worked with the University of Namibia Library and the National Archives of Namibia and has repatriated collections to the latter since 1995. The page gives no access or visiting terms. I did not open the archive catalogue or any finding aid, so the holdings are not described here.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English home page on 2026-11-08; the /en/archive/ address guessed from the menu returned 404. Wikidata search for the name returns Q23783862 described as a publishing company, so I left the id null.

providers.name: University of Namibia Archives (UNAM Archives online catalogue)
providers.what: The online catalogue of the University of Namibia Archives, set up in 1994, in the basement of the Main Library in Windhoek. It holds university records since 1992, records of former education and agricultural colleges, and private collections on Namibian history, politics, language and religion. Ten named collections are listed, including one from the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran Mission. The catalogue can be browsed by descriptions, places, subjects and digital objects and has basic and advanced search. Business records over 30 years old can be used in the reading room under the Archives Act of 1992, and private collections are viewed in person. The older archives.unam.na address has a certificate mismatch, so the .edu.na address is used.
providers.triageNote: Opened the catalogue home page on 2026-11-08; did not search it. The host archives.unam.na failed with a certificate name mismatch, so the .edu.na host was used.

providers.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina (Alexandria, Egypt)
providers.what: The library of Alexandria, whose home page lists digital collections including Memory of Modern Egypt, the digitised Description de l'Egypte, the CEDEJ Egyptian press archive, Memory of the Suez Canal and archives relating to three presidents, plus a Digital Assets Repository. Physical holdings named are a microforms and exchange section, rare books, a map library, theses and a Manuscripts Center. The page gives reading-room hours (Sunday to Thursday, Saturday mornings, closed Friday), an Ask a Librarian service and an online catalogue. It does not say whether the digital collections are free to use or which newspapers are digitised, and I did not open them.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English home page on 2026-11-08 and read the menu; sub-collections were not opened (the Memory of Modern Egypt address returned only a redirect page). Wikidata Q501851 matched (major library and cultural centre in Alexandria).

providers.name: Liberated Africans (liberatedafricans.org)
providers.what: A digital resource on 'liberated Africans', people declared free after the slave trade was suppressed but then indentured by governments, said to number over 700,000 between 1800 and 1920. The home page lists sections for court records, legislation, laws and treaties, courts and cases, and a People database. It names Walk With Web Inc. and the Digital Slavery Research Lab (University of Colorado) as sponsors or partners and cites two journal articles on the underlying data. The page does not say which courts or registers are included or how the People database is searched, and it states no access terms. I did not open the databases.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read its section list and sponsor line; the People database and court records were not opened.

providers.name: Nigeria Genealogy and Biographies Foundation (nigeriagenealogy.ng)
providers.what: A publicly browsable genealogy site on TNG software run by the Nigeria Genealogy and Biographies Foundation, which says it aims to become Nigeria's largest repository of genealogical records. It has family trees grouped by ethnic group (Igbo, Hausa, Yoruba), biographical profiles and history articles, media categories (photos, documents, headstones, histories, recordings), and reference lists of surnames, first names, places, cemeteries, sources and repositories. Search is by name, family or site, with browse pages by surname and place. The page has a Login link but does not say what needs one, and it does not give record counts, so I cannot say how much is indexed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not run a search or open any tree.

providers.name: Friends of St Helena (registered charity, research resources and journals)
providers.what: A registered charity founded in 1988 that publishes the St Helena Connection magazine twice a year and the annual history journal Wirebird, with books under the Wirebird imprint such as a volume of 1678-1683 St Helena records. Its 'About St Helena' section lists reports and statistics, colonial annual reports, a library, the Kitching and Hearl Papers and a links directory. Members get free magazines, online archive access and discounts. The site advertises a St Helena Ancestors database, which has its own row. The page does not state what part of the archive is open to non-members.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Access class 'mixed' reflects a members' benefits list plus public pages; the member-only extent was not tested.

providers.name: St Helena Ancestors (Friends of St Helena database)
providers.what: The ancestry database of the Friends of St Helena, a search form for forename and surname with optional start and end years, where each name field can be set to begins with, exact, anywhere or ends with. Results show forename, surname, year and a database column. The page does not say which records or years are in the database or whether the full details need payment; a FIBIS wiki page I read says the data came from transcribed parish registers, initial searches are free and full details need paid membership, but I did not confirm that on the database page itself. The page shows a Sign In link.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08; did not search. Free-versus-paid statement comes from a secondary FIBIS wiki page (wiki.fibis.org/w/St_Helena), not from this page.

providers.name: Généalogie Algérie Maroc Tunisie (GAMT)
providers.what: A French association, with headquarters in Aix-en-Provence and eight regional branches, for tracing ancestors who lived in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia in the French period (1830 to 1962). Its home page says members can use about four million indexed records, a name search box, help with research and a searchable quarterly magazine. A French genealogy news item says volunteers indexed the 1922 civil registers that the Archives nationales d'outre-mer put online, covering named communes in all three countries, and that anyone can search by surname but detailed results are for members only. The home page says GAMT's own archives stayed in North Africa.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and a RFgenealogie news article on the 1922 index on 2026-11-08. The 'Fonds relevés' address from the article returned 404, so the list of indexed collections was not read.

providers.name: SephardicGen (Sephardic genealogy resource, North Africa and Egypt sections)
providers.what: A personal Sephardic genealogy site by Jeff Malka with sections on research methods, websites by country, Sephardic family trees, a gazetteer, surname lists, a bibliography, archives and a databases section. Region pages include Egypt, Morocco and North Africa, plus Spain, Portugal, Turkey, Greece, Iraq and others. The databases are hosted at sephardicgen.com/databases, and the site shows no login or fee, though its books are sold separately. I read the home page and three of its Egypt and Morocco pages; the 'North Africa' page address I guessed returned 404, so Algeria, Tunisia and Libya coverage is unconfirmed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Separate rows cover its Egypt, Morocco and two Egypt databases. The author's name appears on the site as the creator; no other person is named here.

providers.name: SephardicGen: Egypt records, archives and databases page
providers.what: A guide page for Egyptian Jewish research. It lists archives (the Jewish community offices in Cairo and Alexandria, described as restricted and disorganised, Egyptian civil authorities, and the Alliance Israelite Universelle archive in Paris) and databases hosted on the site: the 1942-43 Annuaire des Juifs d'Egypte, the 1941 Egyptian Directory, an annotated index of a 1938 book on the Jews of Egypt, Egyptian Jews deported from France in the Second World War, and those who died in camps. It also links off-site items such as an 1840 Alexandria census PDF, 1934-35 Alexandria marriage authorisations, and archived cemetery and synagogue photo pages. I opened none of the linked databases except the two with their own rows.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08. Many linked pages are web.archive.org copies. I did not follow the off-site links.

providers.name: Annuaire des Juifs d'Egypte 1942-43, prominent Jews index (SephardicGen)
providers.what: A free web search form giving an annotated index of the list of prominent Jews printed at the end of the 1942 and 1943 Annuaire des Juifs d'Egypte, one of only two yearbooks of Egyptian Jewry. It holds 189 persons: scholars, tradesmen, rabbis, bankers, civil servants and others, each with a short biography and sometimes a photo in the book. Search is by surname and given name with contains, exact, sounds-like, starts-with and ends-with options. The page does not say whether the biographies or photos are viewable online. It is an index of one printed list, not of community registers.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search form page on 2026-11-08; did not run a search.

providers.name: Egypt Directory 1941: Jewish names index (SephardicGen)
providers.what: A free search form for an index of Jewish names in the 1941 Egypt Directory, the 55th edition of a directory published since 1887. The page says the directory was found and scanned by volunteers and a researcher then identified the Jewish names for the index. Search is by surname and given name with five match types, and the page says Jews appear in about 300 listed professions. It does not give the number of entries, and it does not say whether the scanned directory pages can be viewed. A set of scans is linked on a separate photo site per the Egypt guide page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search form page on 2026-11-08; did not search.

providers.name: SephardicGen: Morocco records, archives and databases page
providers.what: A guide page for Moroccan Jewish research, noting that Morocco kept almost no government civil registration, so sources are community, institutional and cemetery records. It names archives (community registers from Casablanca, Fes, Meknes, Mogador and Sefrou for 1710 to 1963 in Jerusalem, French civil records for Morocco in the diplomatic archives at Nantes, and Alliance Israelite Universelle school records in Paris) and databases on the site, including Jews of Morocco deported from France, a Meknes collection of over 22,000 family trees, an index of Moroccan rabbis and an index of Essaouira marriage contracts for 1789 to 2003. It also links off-site cemetery lists for Essaouira, Tangier and Tetuan and a bibliography. I opened none of the linked items.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08; the descriptions are the page's own, none of the databases was opened.

providers.name: L'Aurore Alexandria Jewish Community Births, Marriages and Deaths 1933-1941 (JewishGen)
providers.what: A JewishGen database indexing birth, marriage and death announcements from the Alexandria Jewish community printed in the French-language weekly L'Aurore, 1933 to 1941, with 1938 missing because those issues are not in the source collection. It lists about 2,400 entries, each giving record type, surname, given name, the week of registration, parents' or spouse's names where printed, and the issue number. It can be searched through the JewishGen Egypt database, the Sephardic collection or Unified Search. The page states no fee. It is an index of a newspaper's notices, not of the community registers themselves.
providers.triageNote: Opened the database description page on 2026-11-08; did not run a search. JewishGen already has other rows; this is a distinct database.

providers.name: Indische Genealogische Vereniging (IGV), society for Dutch East Indies genealogy
providers.what: Dutch society for research into families from the former Dutch East Indies (Indonesia) and related colonies. Its site has a menu of source guides: a search guide and advice section, pages on the Nationaal Archief holdings relevant to the Indies, on Delpher, on the Indonesian national archives (ANRI) and on LDS microfilm, plus a page pointing to an index of publications on former Dutch burial and memorial grounds in Indonesia. The 'Indisch Archief' page describes the society's own archive of about 30 collections with over two million records and more than 100,000 images, held on the archieven.nl platform; using it needs a free archieven.nl account and verification of IGV membership. Other members-only material includes a publications set on USB and the journal 'Indische Navorscher' (an index of the 1988-2007 series is listed). I read the home page and three source pages; I did not open the archive itself, the index of burial grounds, or the journal index.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Indisch Archief, Begraaf- en Gedenkplaatsen and Nationaal Archief pages on 2026-11-08. Did not log in, did not test the archive search, did not check membership fees. The Nationaal Archief and Delpher themselves are existing rows.

providers.name: Dutch Burgher Union of Ceylon (DBU), Colombo
providers.what: Community association of the Burgher people of Sri Lanka (descendants of Dutch and other European settlers), founded 1908 and based in Colombo. Its 'Journals & Genealogies' page says the archive of the society's journal runs from 1908 to 2005 (volumes 1 to 70), has been digitised as searchable PDFs, and carries genealogies of over 200 Burgher families. The page offers separate 'Journals' and 'Genealogies' entries; I saw the headings but did not open the PDF files themselves, so I cannot say how they are searched or whether they are free to download. The rest of the site is about the club, guest rooms, a children's home and a cafe, which are not records.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Journals & Genealogies page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the journal PDFs or the genealogies, so scope per family and any restrictions are unknown.

providers.name: The Anglo-Burmese Library (colonial-era Burma family records)
providers.what: Membership-based website that collects and indexes records and histories of families in colonial-era Burma, and keeps the lists of the 1942 evacuation from Burma. The home page lists transcriptions of church records and ecclesiastical returns from Burma for various years between 1846 and 1994, a probate index 1857 to 1957, and transcriptions of Burma entries in Thacker's directories for various years 1844 to 1941, the Maulmain Directory 1844, and the Civil List for 1938 to 1942. It also lists documents from the Myanmar National Archives indexed on its own database (naturalisation applications, gazette notices), cemetery photographs and inscriptions, digital images of the Moulmein Chronicle 1837 to 1844 with extracts from other Burma papers, company and school pages, military records and a photograph gallery. There is a separate non-members area (trek out of Burma, casualty list, military and public-works material) and a members' area; I did not see which parts need membership beyond the site's own statement, and I did not log in or test a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; the non-members link comes from the FIBIS wiki Burma page and the site menu, not opened separately. Did not test any search or the membership terms.

providers.name: Koi-Hai (Assam and North East India British tea planters site)
providers.what: Free community website about the people who worked in Assam and North East India in tea, river ferry service, oil, research and administration. The menu lists a 'Tea Planters of the past' directory, an Assam directory, a Koi-Hai directory with old newsletters, member stories A to Z, articles on planters' clubs and tea companies, an archives section, a 'Ancestry in India: how to search' guide, a BACSA cemeteries page, and a photo gallery (the home page says all photos are before 1970). I read the home page and its menu only; I did not open the directories, so I cannot say how many people they list or which years they cover.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (the address is http in the site's own links; the https form is used here). Did not open the directories or newsletters.

providers.name: FIBIS Gallery (photographs of British India)
providers.what: Photo gallery run on Piwigo software by the Families in British India Society. The home page shows 4,188 photographs in albums: personal collections (3,441 photos in 53 sub-albums), buildings, military, people, ephemera, railways, and graves, monuments and memorials. Browsing is by album, by a tag cloud of about 1,500 tags (places such as Kashmir, Peshawar, Lahore, Calcutta, Madras, and themes such as churches, railways and the Indian Army), by search, or by recent and random views. The page shows a sign-in option but nothing says viewing needs it; I did not open individual photographs or check whether captions name people.
providers.triageNote: Opened the gallery home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open any album or test viewing without login. The society's main database is an existing row (fibis); this is the separate gallery host.

providers.name: FIBIwiki (Families in British India Society research wiki)
providers.what: Free-to-read wiki described on its front page as an encyclopaedia of life in British India, roughly 1600 to 1947. Its browse list covers birth, marriage and death records, church records, cemeteries, churches, schools, occupations, railways, military topics (armies, regiments, medals, forts), naval and maritime topics, migration, presidencies and locations, non-British ancestors, and research methods such as DNA and recommended reading. The article on India Office Records says they hold the pre-1947 administrative archives of the East India Company, Board of Control, India Office and Burma Office, are held at the British Library, and can be searched through the British Library archive catalogue, TNA Discovery and an India Office family search database of about 300,000 brief records. It also names Findmypast, the Qatar Digital Library and the FIBIS database as online routes. The wiki is a guide to where records are; it is not a record set itself. Pages for Burma, Ceylon, Malaysia and the Straits Settlements list further sources, which I read only in part.
providers.triageNote: Opened the wiki front page, the India Office Records article and the Burma, Ceylon, Dutch Indies and Straits Settlements articles on 2026-11-08. Did not check every article; some linked addresses (for example the India Office family search site) did not answer from my network.

providers.name: anglo-indians.com (Anglo-Indian community history and research pages)
providers.what: Community website about Anglo-Indians with sections for history (classes of Anglo-Indians, names, historical dates), associations by country, schools in alphabetical pages, libraries and museums, publications, reunions, media and biographies of well-known Anglo-Indians. A 'Research' section has pages for Australia, Canada, England and the UK, France, India, Ireland, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa and the USA, and pages for publications, websites, associations and research in progress. I saw the section names and a news feed whose latest entries are old; I did not open the research pages, so I cannot say whether they hold record lists or only links.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 via the page reader. Research and schools pages not opened; the feed suggests content may be dated.

providers.name: Registrar General's Department, Sri Lanka (civil registration and online certificate requests)
providers.what: Government department that keeps civil registration of births, marriages and deaths in Sri Lanka. The English home page lists service pages for birth, marriage, death and translation, a tool for finding the registrar for an area, and an online service to request copies of birth, marriage and death certificates through a separate portal (online.ebmd.rgd.gov.lk). The page text I could read does not state which years the registers cover, how to apply from abroad, or what identifying details a request needs. I did not use the request portal.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (reader summary of the Online Services list). Did not open the birth/marriage/death pages or the portal; years covered and fees unknown.

providers.name: Taiwan History Digital Library (THDL), National Taiwan University
providers.what: Full-text database of primary sources for Taiwan history, built by National Taiwan University from holdings of the NTU Library and the National Taichung Library. The home page says it currently contains three document sets: the Danxin Archives, the Ming-Qing administrative archives of Taiwan, and old land and contract documents, with over 100,000 full-text records, searchable by full text and by metadata. It also has a set of research tools (reference works, analysis tools, tools that rebuild relationships between documents). The interface is in Traditional Chinese; I did not run a search or check whether images are shown, and the page does not say whether use is free.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not search or open any document set.

providers.name: Taiwan Memory (Taiwan Ji Yi), National Central Library
providers.what: Portal of the National Central Library that gathers digitised cultural and historical material about Taiwan from the library and partner institutions. The page shows a search box with an advanced search (title, subject, description, source, publisher, person, all fields) and a synonym option, browsing by category, subject, timeline and map, a Taiwan chronology, and a section of co-built resources from partners. A counter on the page gives about 5.2 million digital objects. Recent news mentions digitisation agreements with a school and a theological college. I did not run a search, so I cannot say which items are family-history records (photographs, documents, newspapers) or what the reuse terms are.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Page is in Chinese with an English switch; no search tried.

providers.name: Digital Jangseogak, Academy of Korean Studies (Joseon royal library holdings)
providers.what: Online viewer for the holdings of Jangseogak, the royal library collection of the Joseon dynasty, kept by the Academy of Korean Studies. Items can be browsed by type, subject or collection, or found through a whole-site or advanced search; royal old books and royal archival documents come with a commentary and original page images. The popular-search list on the home page includes clan genealogy terms (one is named as a clan genealogy), so family books are among the material searched. Nothing on the page mentions a login. The site is in Korean (with Chinese characters in titles); I did not open an item to see the image viewer or reuse terms.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; no item opened. Whether all images are free to view and download is untested.

providers.name: Okinawa Prefectural Archives (Okinawa-ken Komonjokan)
providers.what: Prefectural archives for Okinawa. Its holdings pages name the Ryukyu Government documents (the postwar government before 1972), Okinawa Prefecture documents, materials collected from US sources (including USCAR photographs), and collections of papers on Okinawa; there is a Ryukyu Government Documents Digital Archive. Search pages cover the holdings catalogue, photographs, films, aerial photographs (an item dated 10 December 1945 is announced), audio, official gazettes and lists of transferred documents. The reading room needs a reservation, made by phone or from a calendar on the site. The site is in Japanese; I did not run a catalogue search or open the digital archive, and I cannot say whether the Okinawa wartime or prewar family registers are among the holdings.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (it showed a notice of a planned service suspension on 19-20 November 2026). No search run; the digital archive was not opened.

providers.name: Hong Kong Government Reports Online (HKGRO), University of Hong Kong Libraries
providers.what: Full-text image database of Hong Kong government publications run by the University of Hong Kong Libraries. The page lists administrative reports, Hong Kong Sessional Papers, Hong Kong Hansard, the Hong Kong Government Gazette, the Blue Book and annual reports of departments and committees, with a further section of other government publications. Search is across all content or by title, keyword or creator. The page I read does not give the years covered or say whether use is free (there is a login link). For a family historian the Gazette and the civil service lists are the likely hooks; I did not open any volume to check what names appear.
providers.triageNote: Opened the HKGRO front page on 2026-11-08. Did not search; years and access terms unconfirmed.

providers.name: Gwulo: Old Hong Kong
providers.what: Community-built website of old Hong Kong history. The home page says there are over 60,000 pages, including over 40,000 photographs, added by contributors, plus a weekly 'what is new' post, a newsletter and a note about the historic map site hkmaps.hk (searchable by building address and lot number). It is useful for places, buildings, streets and wartime history, and its pages are often visited by people tracing relatives who lived or were interned in the colony. I read the home page only and did not open a place, photo or people page, so I cannot say how names are indexed or how reliable individual entries are.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not test searching for a name.

providers.name: FamilySearch Online Jiapu Search (Chinese clan genealogy books)
providers.what: Search page for FamilySearch's collection of Chinese jiapu (clan genealogy books), which the page puts at more than 65,000 books. The search can be run by surname, ancestral village, ancestral hall name, first ancestor's name or generation name. The page says the family trees can be viewed free once a free FamilySearch account is created. The page is in English with a link to a Traditional Chinese version. I did not sign in or run a search, so I cannot say what a result list looks like or how many books are indexed to village level.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08 without signing in. The limit or restrictions on viewing images are not stated on the page.

providers.name: Western Pacific Archives, University of Auckland (He Mara Mahara)
providers.what: Archive of the British colonial administration of the Western Pacific from 1877 to 1978, transferred to the University of Auckland Library in 2002: records of the Western Pacific High Commission, the British Agent and Consul in Tonga, and the New Hebrides British Service, about 2,800 boxes. The repository description says the files include maps, photographs, passport applications, probate files and registers of various types. The collection list (124 collections) begins with Tonga correspondence (such as records of 1874 to 1968 including passport applications and estate papers), High Commissioner's Court records, and inward correspondence registers and indexes 1875 to 1946. A subject entry shows a Western Pacific High Commission birth register volume for 1922 to 1944 on microfilm. It is a catalogue (ArchivesSpace) of paper and film; I did not see any images online and did not read the remaining collections.
providers.triageNote: Opened the repository page, the first page of the collection list (15 of 124) and one subject page on 2026-11-08. The other 109 collections were not read, so registers of births, deaths and marriages for other territories are unconfirmed.

providers.name: Micronesian Area Research Center (MARC), University of Guam
providers.what: Research library and archive at the University of Guam for Guam and Micronesia. Its page describes more than 40,000 volumes, about 800 theses, over 100,000 pages of Spanish-era documents, about 23,000 photographic prints with 90,000 negatives, maps, manuscripts and a CHamoru genealogy collection with over 100 family genealogies. Opening hours are listed for the Guam and Micronesia Collection and for the manuscripts and Spanish documents, where one person is admitted at a time; Tuesday and Wednesday hours are marked for genealogy users. A library catalogue and a separate digital-collections address are named. I did not open either, so it is not known which items are online.
providers.triageNote: Opened the MARC page on 2026-11-08. Catalogue and digital collections not opened; hours on the page may be out of date (it mentions a vaccination form).

providers.name: Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site and Archives (library and digital archive)
providers.what: Library and archive of the Hawaiian Mission Children's Society at Honolulu. The page describes digital collections of letters, journals and publications of the American Board mission, including items written or printed at the Honolulu mission station, and says the library holds an extensive collection of Hawaiian-language publications. A catalogue is on LibraryWorld, scans are on an Omeka site, and virtual exhibits are on PastPerfect. The main menu has a 'Genealogy and Cemetery' entry that I saw but whose contents I did not open. The reading room is by reservation only, with office hours on weekdays. I did not use the catalogue or the digital archive, whose host did not answer from my network.
providers.triageNote: Opened the library/archives page and the site front page on 2026-11-08. The Omeka digital archive (hmha.missionhouses.org) timed out; not read.

providers.name: Hawaii State Archives: Ships' Passenger Manifests 1843-1921
providers.what: Page of the Hawaii State Archives on its collection of passenger manifests for arrivals at Hawaiian ports. The Archives has indexed manifests from 1843 to 1900, arranged by nationality and then alphabetically by surname, with a separate surname index for 1880 to 1900 and further indexes still being scanned; it also holds a copy of manifests for February 1900 to January 1921 in date order. The microfilms generally show name, age, occupation, family members, country of origin, dates, ship and port. For 1900 to 1916 only foreign arrivals are covered, and after 1900 immigration records moved to the federal service. Scans are said to be in the Digital Archives under passenger arrivals and departures (1843 to 1900) and passenger lists (1900 to 1921); some indexes are in the Research Room only. I did not open the scans.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the Digital Archives scans; cost of the online scans not stated.

providers.name: Hawaiian Historical Society (research library and publications)
providers.what: Historical society in Honolulu with a research library, an online catalogue and a long-running publications programme. The site menu lists the Hawaiian Journal of History with indexes to it, annual reports, papers of the society, a Hawaiian-language reprint series, the research library page, a catalogue, forms and a 'beaches of Hawaii' image collection. I saw the menu and the library entries but did not open them, so I cannot say what manuscripts, photographs or genealogical material the library holds or whether the catalogue lists names.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; the research-library and catalogue pages were not opened (a guessed research-library address returned 404).

providers.name: AUB Libraries Digital Collections, American University of Beirut
providers.what: Digital collections of the American University of Beirut libraries. The first listing page names the Lebanese Newspapers Digital Archive, a Palestinian Oral History Archive with over 1,000 hours of testimony from Palestinians in Lebanon, a Gender Oral History Archive, about 1,800 mostly Arabic manuscripts, Arabic books online, the Arabic literary magazine Al-Adab 1953 to 2012, an early Arabic medical journal, and a collection on Arabic cinema and theatre with photographs 1913 to 1952. The page does not give dates or languages for the newspaper archive, and a second listing page exists that I did not read. The Archives and Special Collections page was also opened but was mostly site navigation.
providers.triageNote: Opened the digital-collections listing (page 1) on 2026-11-08; no collection opened, so searching and access terms are unknown.

providers.name: IGRA: Ottoman-period databases (to 1917)
providers.what: Category page of the Israel Genealogy Research Association listing its Ottoman-period name databases, as examples and not a full list. Groups include births (British consulate registers for Jaffa, a Jerusalem Christ Church baptism register), burials (Safed old and new cemeteries), founders and settlers of colonies (Petah Tikva, Zikhron Ya'akov, Rehovot), immigrants, kolel (community charity) lists 1889 to 1918, Jerusalem marriages 1893 to 1913, newspaper lists, two Jerusalem nufus population registers (1890 and 1910), a home for the aged 1823 to 1903, and school lists. Counts are given per database. The page says free registration gives fuller access to the more than a million records on the site; I did not register or search, so what a non-member sees is unknown.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08 without registering. This is a sub-page of the existing IGRA row (igra-israel-genealogy-research-association).

providers.name: IGRA: British Mandate databases (Palestine 1917-1948)
providers.what: Page of the Israel Genealogy Research Association listing databases from the British Mandate period, again as examples. They include a Tel Aviv census of 1922 (13,262 residents), voters' lists 1922 to 1946 for several towns (Haifa 1942 has over 44,000 names), name changes 1922 to 1948 from the Palestine Gazette (over 27,000), lists of Jewish Legion and WWII volunteers, immigration and deportation lists 1919 to 1948, local birth, death and marriage registers (for example Zikhron Ya'akov and Pardes Hana), telephone and medical-practitioner directories, and school rosters. Several are marked as work in progress, and some say the original is held in another archive. The page links to the main search at genealogy.org.il/AID/ and gives no single search method; free registration is mentioned on the sister pages.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08; the last part of the page (about 10,000 characters) was not read and no search was run.

providers.name: IGRA guide to the Ottoman nufus (population) registers of Palestine, 1879-1917
providers.what: Research guide with two searchable tables, one of the registers and one of the microfilms, to the Ottoman nufus population registers for the districts of Palestine. The guide explains seven register types (early, preliminary and basic population books, men of military age, foreigners, mukhtar's books, and registers of births, marriages, deaths and divorces), dates from 1876 with most from about 1884, calendar conversion, and the religious community groupings used in the books. It says most registers are in Ottoman Turkish and few have Hebrew, that about 463 are known and 460 were microfilmed in 1964 and 1969 on 82 films, and that the Israel State Archives has scanned the films and posted them on its site. The tables are a finding aid and not a name index. I read the guide; I did not test the State Archives scans, which are on a site that refuses scripted access.
providers.triageNote: Opened the guide on 2026-11-08 (page text about 155,000 characters; first 100,000 read). The ISA scans were not checked; archives.gov.il returns 403 to scripts and was not tried further.

providers.name: Montefiore Censuses of the Jews of the Land of Israel, 1839-1875 (Montefiore Endowment)
providers.what: Searchable index of the censuses of Jewish communities taken for Moses Montefiore in 1839, 1840, 1849, 1855, 1866 and 1875. The search page offers a simple name search and an advanced search with filters for year, residence (Safed, Jerusalem, Hebron, Tiberias, Jaffa, Haifa, Acre, Ramla, Beirut and others), kolel (community), country and place of birth, occupation and economic status, with results for families or institutions in English or Hebrew. A family entry carries each person's name, age, status, place of birth, year of arrival and occupation, with a link to a PDF scan. A sample search showed over 26,000 matches. The old address (montefiorecensuses.org) redirects here. The page does not say whether use is free.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08 (reached from the redirect of the old montefiorecensuses.org address). Ran no search of my own.

providers.name: Houshamadyan (reconstructing Ottoman Armenian town and village life)
providers.what: Digital project in English, Armenian and Turkish that rebuilds the history of Ottoman Armenian towns and villages. Content is organised by Ottoman administrative units (vilayet, sanjak, kaza), with town pages that cover topics such as demography, dialects, monasteries and pilgrimage, plus maps, thematic sections, a music library, a video library, family collections and a 'Voices' section. The page does not describe a name database or family trees, so it is best for the place and community background of an ancestor from a named town, and for finding contributed family collections. I read the home page only; I did not open a town page, so how deep each place is remains unknown, and the page does not state terms of use.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. No town page opened; shop and support pages exist.

providers.name: National Archives of Thailand (Krom Sinlapakon, Fine Arts Department)
providers.what: Thai national archive. The home page describes written archival records and audiovisual records, a valued photo collection (royal events, scout gatherings of the 1920s to 1940s), glass-plate negatives, a Memory of the World register, e-books, videos and a mobile app. Online systems named are an archive search system (archives.nat.go.th), a records-management system, Memory of the World registration and a photo-description project. Reading-room hours are given for written records (Monday to Saturday) and audiovisual records (Monday to Friday). The page is in Thai and does not say what the search system covers or whether images are provided online; I did not open the search system.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (reader summary of the Thai page). The archive search system was not opened.

providers.name: Digital South Asia Library (DSAL), University of Chicago
providers.what: University of Chicago portal of online resources on South Asia. The home page groups them into reference works and digital dictionaries, bibliographies and union lists, images (photograph databases arranged by original collection), periodical indexes, maps (historical to topographic), books and journals including newspapers, and statistics from the colonial period onward. A recent entry presents the Linguistic Survey of India gramophone recordings. The page does not say which reference works are included or whether any item is behind a login; I did not open a category, so I cannot confirm gazetteers or census reports, which the Atlas could use for place names.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. No category opened.

providers.name: Roja Muthiah Research Library, Chennai (Tamil culture library and archive)
providers.what: Library, archive, museum and research centre for Tamil culture, founded 1994 in Chennai. The home page says it holds about 500,000 items and has digitally preserved over 3 million page images, with a digital library reached through a 'Browse Digital Library' link, a catalogue search, and a visit page. The page does not break down the holdings (books, periodicals, ephemera) or say which years are covered. I did not open the digital library or the catalogue, so I cannot say what is free to read or whether it holds family or community records.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Digital library and catalogue not opened.

providers.name: Leiden University Libraries Digital Collections (KITLV and Asian collections)
providers.what: Digital collections of Leiden University Libraries. The collection menu includes the KITLV collections (Dutch East Indies literature, colonial archives, maps, Southeast Asian and Caribbean images, oral history), KIT colonial journals, colonial sources and Dutch colonial maps, Indonesian printed resources and serials, and photo albums and prints. Image, text and map collections can be browsed or searched, and a help page explains use. The site says copyright material may have access limits and that it is moving to a new system. I did not open a collection, so I do not know whether any list people by name, or whether images can be downloaded.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and its collection selector on 2026-11-08. Terms of use page not read.

providers.name: Archives de la Nouvelle-Caledonie (Noumea)
providers.what: Territorial archive service of New Caledonia in Nouville, Noumea. The home page has a genealogy section under its research menu, a list of holdings that includes civil registration, links to online archive and library searches, and a sample notarial deed of 1877. The service is open to the public Tuesday to Friday and Saturday mornings. The page does not say which years the civil registers cover, whether images are online, or whether convict (penal colony) files are held here; I did not open the genealogy section or the searches.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 via the page reader. Genealogy pages and search tools not opened.

providers.name: BIGKinds (Korea Press Foundation news archive and search)
providers.what: News search and analysis service run by the Korea Press Foundation in Seoul. The page reports over 119 million articles collected, from well over a hundred outlets including national dailies, broadcasters, economic papers, regional papers and online outlets. Search supports operators and exact phrases, and advanced filters for period, outlet, category and incident type; browsing includes a historical newspaper archive section. Search periods are limited (five years with a keyword), and saved searches and alerts need a login. The page does not give the earliest year of coverage; it links to a table of coverage by year that I did not open. The text is Korean.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (reader summary). Did not use the historical archive; earliest year unknown.

providers.name: National Library of Korea (Seoul/Sejong)
providers.what: National library of South Korea. Its catalogue search offers fields for title, author (with authority records), publisher, keyword, year and classification numbers, including older Japanese-era schemes. The menus show material types for old books (with a reading room), newspapers, articles, serials, theses, microforms, maps, images, local-history items, overseas records and a North Korea materials centre, and links to a union catalogue of Korean old books, a national repository and a web archive. I read only the first part of a very long page and did not search, so I cannot say which newspapers or years are digitised, or whether clan genealogies (jokbo) are catalogued.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (reader summary of the first 100,000 characters). No search run.

providers.name: National Library of India, Kolkata
providers.what: National library of India in Kolkata. The home page links an online catalogue (OPAC), lists of journals and newspapers received under the Delivery of Books and Newspapers Act, lists of online and foreign journals, a rare and other collections section, and digitised books and documents hosted on the government's Indian Culture portal. It names the library as one of four that receive copies of publications under the 1954 Act. The page does not mention genealogy material and I did not open the rare collections or digital pages; membership is open to citizens over 18 by electronic form.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 via the page reader. Catalogue and digital pages not opened; a library notice mentioned OPAC downtime in December 2025.

providers.name: The Asiatic Society of Mumbai (Town Hall library and manuscripts)
providers.what: Learned society and library in Mumbai. The site menu lists holdings (books, periodicals, manuscripts, coins and Sopara relics), a computerisation page, an online catalogue, and a digital portal named ASM Granth Sanjeevani. It also lists a journal (volume 92 announced for the society's 220th foundation day in November 2024), lectures, research fellowships and membership. A notice on the home page warns that the society does not charge for publishing papers. I read the home page and menu only, so what the manuscripts and periodicals contain, and whether the catalogue is open to non-members, is not known.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Online catalogue and Granth Sanjeevani not opened.

providers.name: SOAS Special Collections (University of London)
providers.what: Special collections of the SOAS library: the page describes over 3 kilometres of archives and about 60,000 rare books and manuscripts in more than 140 languages, covering Africa, Asia and the Middle East and British interaction with them over about 250 years. It links to a visit-booking page, library catalogues and SOAS Digital Collections. The page does not name the missionary archives (for example mission society records) that SOAS is known to hold, and I did not confirm them from the SOAS site; ask the special collections team about a particular mission or region. I did not use the catalogues.
providers.triageNote: Opened the special-collections landing page on 2026-11-08. Mission archive pages (guessed address) returned 404; not read.

providers.name: SOAS Digital Collections
providers.what: Digital collections of SOAS, University of London, organised under Library, Archives, Manuscripts and Art and Objects, and including the Tsinghua Digitisation Project (about 7,000 items, 16th to 20th century). The site covers Asia, Africa and the Middle East and offers search boxes, advanced search, a browse overview, an A to Z list of collections, and filters by language, topic, date, resource type and repository. A free optional account saves searches and documents. The page does not name mission archives or photograph sets, and I did not open a collection or check which items are free to download.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. No collection opened.

providers.name: Brisbane City Archives (Brisbane City Council)
providers.what: The historical records office of Brisbane City Council. Its page lists what can be searched online: historic photographs from 1911 to 2000, Council minutes and annual reports, historic maps and plans from the 1860s, and planning and building records from before 1982, plus house-history advice. Items held on paper are found through the Brisbane Libraries catalogue (eLibcat). The reading room is in the suburb of Moorooka and keeps limited weekday hours with appointments for other times. It is mainly a source for properties, streets and council business rather than for named individuals; the page also points to a separate council cemetery grave search for burials. I did not run a catalogue search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the Brisbane City Archives page on 2026-11-08 with a plain HTTP fetch and read the sections on searching, contact and FAQs. Did not use eLibcat or the online collection.

providers.name: Brisbane City Archives online collection (Recollect)
providers.what: The online catalogue and digital collection of Brisbane City Archives, hosted on a Recollect site. The front page shows featured collections including Council minutes 1925 to 2020 (post-amalgamation, with pre-1925 minutes in a separate collection), a Detail Plans search guide and index (sewerage-era plans with contour levels), Early Houses and Properties 1880 to 1920, and an Archivist's Picks selection. A house-history guide and a Browse All page are linked, and there are login and register links. Useful mainly for houses, streets and local government, and the minutes name councillors and ratepayers in the course of business. I did not run a search or open any item images.
providers.triageNote: Opened the Recollect home page on 2026-11-08 and read the featured collections text. Did not log in, search or open a record.

providers.name: Queensland Family History Society (QFHS)
providers.what: The state family-history society for Queensland, based in Brisbane and formed in 1979. Its home page lists searchable datasets (a global keyword search, datasets by category and a members' interests index) and searchable collections: Queensland cemetery transcripts arranged by region, regional collections for Far North, North, Central, Darling Downs and South-West, South-East and Wide Bay Burnett, family histories and other works. It also lists a library catalogue, links to MyHeritage and FamilySearch images, and back issues of its journal. The page does not say which of these searches need membership, and I did not run one, so access is unconfirmed.
providers.triageNote: Read the QFHS home page on 2026-11-08. The /datasets address returned 404, so the individual datasets were not opened and no search was run.

providers.name: Queensland State Archives: Australian South Sea Islanders records and indexes
providers.what: A Queensland State Archives page about records of Australian South Sea Islander (Pacific Islander labour) people. It describes the labour trade into Queensland between 1863 and 1904 and lists the kinds of archives held: recruitment and arrival, registers of agreement, employment, education, legal, health and medical issues, deportation and repatriation, and those who stayed after 1906. It links a research guide and three name indexes that can be searched or downloaded in full: Australian South Sea Islanders 1867 to 1948, Coloured labour and Asiatic aliens in Queensland 1913, and Sugar Exemptions 1922 to 1923. I did not run a name search or open a digitised register.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08 and read the record types and the three listed indexes. The research guide PDF was not opened and no index was searched.

providers.name: Queensland Government: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family and personal history service
providers.what: A Queensland Government page for people researching Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family history. It explains that the state holds a large body of historical records created under the Protection Acts from 1897 onward and invites an online Family and Personal History request to the department responsible. It gives advice on where to start, notes that family permission may be asked for sensitive material, warns that records can be distressing and use offensive language, and lists Queensland Government and other organisations that can help. It is a request-based service rather than a searchable index, and I did not submit a request.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08. Did not open or submit the request form, so the processing time and what is released were not seen.

providers.name: Anglican Church Southern Queensland: Records and Archives Centre
providers.what: The page for the Records and Archives Centre of the Anglican Diocese of Brisbane (now Anglican Church Southern Queensland). It says the centre was set up in 1979 as the official repository of diocesan records and explains why church archives matter for local and family history. It lists holdings in general terms: registers, minute books, correspondence, magazines, year books, building plans and photographs, and links to the church chronicles, a diocesan newsletter and lists of bishops. I did not find a name index on this page and did not check opening hours, search tools or what parish registers are included.
providers.triageNote: Read the archives page on 2026-11-08. A second address (brisbane.anglican.org.au) did not load. Nothing was searched.

providers.name: NSW War Memorials Register
providers.what: A crowd-sourced register of war memorials across New South Wales, run by the state government. The home page says it holds more than 3,800 memorial records contributed by the public, veterans' groups, councils and historians. It offers a keyword search with separate memorial and veteran modes, and a search by suburb or postcode, and the listings include honour rolls from schools, churches and businesses. Useful for finding where a name is carved or listed locally. It is a register of memorials rather than of service files, and I did not open a memorial record to see how complete the name lists are.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read its description and search options. No search run.

providers.name: Australian Jewish Historical Society: Burials database
providers.what: A searchable database of Jewish burials in Australia kept by the Australian Jewish Historical Society. The page says it has more than 87,000 records of an estimated 95,000 Jewish burials at about 300 sites, and that it grew from a long transcription project that covered Jewish headstones and burial records in Australia and New Zealand and Australian war graves overseas. Search all burials and a cemetery map are offered. A notice says some content from the old system is still being moved across, and that figures from several sources can conflict, so original records should be checked. I did not run a search.

at.place: Potts Point, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

providers.triageNote: Read the Burials landing page on 2026-11-08 (last-updated line said 5 June 2026). Did not search or view a record.

providers.name: Australian Jewish Historical Society: Communal Archives catalogue
providers.what: The catalogue of the Australian Jewish Historical Society's archives. The page says the Society holds about 40,000 paper records, over 100 objects, 500 audio and audio-visual items, 14,000 photographs and 100 plans, and that the Archive of Australian Judaica was added in 2022. It covers synagogues that no longer exist, minutes and scrapbooks of communal organisations, and the personal papers of community figures, with sections for personal papers, organisations, small donations, audio, photographs and publications. Some organisations' records are restricted and need prior approval. I did not search the catalogue.

providers.name: Catholic Cemeteries + Crematoria (Sydney): Deceased Search
providers.what: The online deceased search of the Catholic cemetery trust in Sydney. providers.name: NSW State Archives: Probate packets and wills guide
providers.what: A guide from the NSW State Archives (Museums of History NSW) to probate records. It explains what a grant of probate is, that not every death produced a packet, and that the archives hold probate packets from 1817 to 1989 with gaps, arranged by the date probate was granted rather than the date of death. Packet contents include the will, codicils, inventories and affidavits. The guide also covers the early probate index for 1790 to 1875, will books from 1800, deceased estate files 1880 to 1959, and UK sources. It notes that birth certificates inside packets are closed for 100 years. I did not search the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; catalogue searches were not run. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Inquests and coronial records guide
providers.what: A guide from the NSW State Archives to inquest records. It separates inquests before 1825 from those for the whole state between 1826 and 1963, and lists indexes and registers, inquest papers and local series. Named indexes are the Index to Colonial Secretary's papers 1788 to 1825, the Coroners inquest index 1796 to 1824, and the Inquest index covering 1851 and 1916 to 1963. It explains that you need a name and approximate year, that a death certificate shows whether an inquest was held, and that some files carry distressing material. Some records are digitised in the catalogue, and Ancestry holds related coroners' registers. I did not search.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; no index searched. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Gaol inmates and prisoners guide
providers.what: A guide from the NSW State Archives to prison records. It explains the changing authorities (Provost Marshal, Sheriff, Department of Prisons) and how to tell whether someone was in a gaol, using court records, police gazettes, death certificates and newspapers. It describes typical record types such as entrance books, description books, photograph description books, discharge books and gaoler's journals, and explains access: records over 70 years old can be seen and newer ones are restricted. I read the guide text only, not the catalogue series lists or any index.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; no series or index opened. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Mental health facilities guide
providers.what: A guide from the NSW State Archives to records of asylums and mental hospitals. It explains the past terminology (lunatic asylum and similar words appear in the records and finding aids), then gives a short administrative history from the 1811 Castle Hill asylum through Liverpool, Tarban Creek (Gladesville) and later hospitals, with an inspector appointed in 1876. It describes control records, indexes, case papers, medical case books and admission files, related Colonial Secretary papers, and where records are held elsewhere, and states how access works. I did not open the catalogue series or test any restriction period.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; series lists in the catalogue not opened. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Infirm and destitute asylums guide

It lists admission and discharge registers and admission cards, and points to Benevolent Society records held elsewhere. I did not see the dates covered by each register or open the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; no register series opened. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: School records guide

I did not search the index or test which registers are open.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; the index was not searched. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Naturalization records guide
providers.what: A guide from the NSW State Archives to naturalization records created by the colony before Commonwealth responsibility began in 1904. The records in the collection run from 1834 to 1903. The guide explains denization before 1849 and the system created by the 1849 Act, who needed naturalization (people born outside the British Empire who wished to vote or own land, so not Irish or Canadian-born), the five-year residence condition, and what the records can reveal about arrival and place of origin. It points to an index and notes that later records are at the National Archives of Australia. I did not search the index.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; no index searched. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.name: NSW State Archives: Census and musters guide

It is a guide to what survives and where, not a name search. I did not open any muster or census transcription.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide on 2026-11-08; no record set opened. The wider State Archives Collection already has its own row.

providers.what: The archive of the Whanganui Regional Museum.
