Visits are by appointment on weekday mornings, access is free, copies carry charges, and the archivist can research for you for a fee after the first half hour. I did not check any finding aid or whether the catalogue is online.
providers.triageNote: Read the Archives Research and Access page on 2026-11-08. The catalogue was not looked for or opened.

providers.name: Alexander Heritage and Research Library, Whanganui District Library
providers.what: The heritage and whakapapa service of Whanganui District Library, housed in the Alexander Library in Queen's Park. The page says the heritage collections hold books, newspapers, photographs, pamphlets and other material about Whanganui people, organisations and events, a special collection of local military archives, and free access to Ancestry Library and Findmypast within the library. Opening hours are weekdays only. I did not open the catalogue or check what is digitised.
providers.triageNote: Read the heritage and whakapapa page on 2026-11-08. No catalogue search.

providers.name: arkiv.dk (Danish local and city archives portal / Indgangen til din Danmarkshistorie)
providers.what: Joint search portal for material held by more than 580 Danish local and city archives and a few special collections. The 'about' page says part of the material is digitised and can be viewed directly on the site, but much is not, and the visitor is told to contact the holding archive. Entries are searched by free text with filters for place, parish, municipality, year and material type (photographs, maps, drawings and so on). Its FAQ advises searching by address or place name, and notes that some class photographs and names are withheld for data protection. The site is run by a company owned by the Danish archives together. I did not run a search or test which images open without an account.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page, 'om', 'faq' and the list of contributing archives on 2026-11-08; no search run, so image access unconfirmed.

providers.name: AarhusArkivet (Aarhus Stadsarkiv digital archive)
providers.what: Digital service of the Aarhus City Archives with about 300,000 documents, films and pictures viewable online, while other items must be ordered to the reading room. Its genealogy guide names person sources: a card index of newspaper extracts (about 95,000 person entries, roughly 1794 to 1950), municipal tax lists digitised with FamilySearch, city directories for 1859-1940 and council records. A tag-based (entity) search lets you search names, and many documents carry such tags while most do not. The guide sends researchers needing pre-1841 material to the national archive's online sources. Each item has an availability label: online, reading room or in store. The site has a login and registration link; I did not log in or test which items need it.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page, 'about the collections', availability and genealogy guide on 2026-11-08; did not search or log in.

providers.name: Aalborg Stadsarkiv (Aalborg City Archives)
providers.what: City archive of Aalborg in north Jutland. The 'use the archive' page says records are ordered by logging in to the national digital-post system with a national electronic ID, giving a purpose, and naming the archive item by its A-number and running number, which are found on the archive's own search page or on arkiv.dk. Some records need special permission to see. The site menu lists search of the collection, city council minutes and a section about the archive. The same host already carries the Danish emigration archive row. I did not open the search page or the council-minutes database, so what is online beyond the ordering route is unchecked.
providers.triageNote: Read the 'Brug Arkivet' page only on 2026-11-08; the search and council-minutes pages were not opened.

providers.name: Danish Family Search (Danskerbasen)
providers.what: Volunteer-run Danish genealogy site with a name database ('Danskerbasen') said on its home page to hold about 41 million entries typed from census returns and church books, with a picture viewer for the original pages. It is organised by Danish county and also lists the Danish West Indies, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, Schleswig-Holstein and ships and abroad. Further sections cover street and place names, conscription rolls (lægdsruller), themes and indexing projects including the 1906 and 1940 censuses. The home page invites free membership to type records, save searches and use the forum. I did not search the database or test what a visitor without an account can see.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; the deeper census and church-book pages I guessed returned 404, so those were not read; no search run.

providers.name: Mindelunden i Ryvangen (Memorial Park for the Danish resistance 1940-1945)
providers.what: War cemetery and memorial in Hellerup, Copenhagen, for Danish resistance members who died during the German occupation, on the former execution and burial ground. The site describes the memorial wall, the main grave field, concentration-camp graves, the execution place and a seamen's memorial, and offers a search for person portraits. Entry to the park is free and guided tours are mentioned. I did not run the person search, so the fields, years and number of portraits are not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; the person search was not run.

providers.name: Dansk Jødisk Museum (Danish Jewish Museum) - genealogy page
providers.what: Museum of 400 years of Danish Jewish history in Copenhagen. Its genealogy page says the collection holds photographs, objects and personal archives relevant to family history, and that purely genealogical enquiries go to the Society for Danish Jewish History. It also points to online databases: Jewish burials and gravestones up to 1886, a Danish-Jewish genealogical database (membership of the society needed) and Jewish men entered in the Copenhagen marriage-licence register 1735-1810. I only read the museum's own pages, not the databases it links to.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and genealogy page on 2026-11-08; linked databases were not opened.

providers.name: Siirtolaisrekisteri (Emigrant Register, Migration Institute of Finland)
providers.what: Database portal of the Migration Institute of Finland in Turku. The institute's genealogy page describes its main databases: a passenger list of about 318,000 records from Finland Steamship Company sailings (1892-1896, 1899-1914, 1920-1960), a passport list of emigrants by province (late 1880s to 1922, with about 100,000 records still to enter), a 19,000-record reference index of obituaries and notices from Finnish-American and other newspapers, plus small databases for Finns in Australia and New Zealand, Finns persecuted in the Soviet Union, Ingrian Finns, forest Finns in Sweden and naturalisations 1832-1946. Further files exist only on paper or are not online. The portal page itself loaded as a script shell; I did not run searches.
providers.triageNote: Read the institute's genealogy and digital-materials pages and the portal landing page on 2026-11-08; searches not run, so terms of access are unconfirmed.

providers.name: Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland (SLS) - archive collections
providers.what: Archive and library of the Society of Swedish Literature in Finland, holding material about life in Swedish in Finland. The collections page lists personal and family archives, farm archives, theatre and society archives, recordings and notes on folk culture, names and language, and many photographs. Search and ordering run through a Finna catalogue at sls.finna.fi, which I did not open. The site also has a page of digital editions and databases. Useful for Swedish-speaking Finnish families, though the page does not say which series list individuals by name.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and archive-collections page on 2026-11-08; the Finna catalogue and databases page were not examined in depth.

providers.name: Byarkivet (Oslo City Archives)
providers.what: City archive of Oslo with a genealogy page listing its sources: nearly 800 metres of municipal census returns for Kristiania and Aker, mainly 1899 to 1954, mostly available in the reading room; the Aker muster roll 1832-1843; Kristiania censuses for 1883 and a run of years 1899-1916; Aker 1917 and Kristiania 1923; address books; parish-boundary and voting lists; poor-relief and home-parish registers; and a 1843-1867 institution list. The page says only a small part has been digitised. Other pages cover building history, maps, Oslo pictures and films. I did not check what is online.
providers.triageNote: Read the Byarkivet front page and its genealogy page on 2026-11-08; the online picture and film sites were not opened.

providers.name: Bergen byarkiv (Bergen City Archives)
providers.what: City archive of Bergen. This site is a collection page for its external online resources: links to its photographs and its digitised minute books on Digitalarkivet, the Bergen city encyclopedia, an Årstad local-history site and a site on the 1916 city fire. The page gives the visiting address and says the reading room is open by appointment on Monday and Tuesday. I followed one link to the encyclopedia but did not open the Digitalarkivet lists, so counts and years of the photographs and protocols are not known.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; the Digitalarkivet photo and protocol searches were not opened.

providers.name: Bergen byleksikon (Bergen city encyclopedia, web edition)
providers.what: Web edition (2013) of the Bergen city encyclopedia, run by Bergen byarkiv. Entries are browsed by letter or by category, with counts shown on the page: for example about 1,920 streets and roads, 650 buildings and properties, 276 farms and pleasure grounds, 193 organisations and associations and 176 religion and denomination entries. The site also describes the printed editions of 1994, 1999 and 2009. Useful for placing an address or institution in Bergen's past. It is a reference work, not a register of persons; I did not read individual entries.
providers.triageNote: Read the encyclopedia front page on 2026-11-08; no entry was opened.

providers.name: Norsk utvandrermuseum (Norwegian Emigrant Museum) - archive
providers.what: Museum at Ottestad in Hedmark whose archive consists of America letters (over 9,000, per the page), private archives, newspaper-cutting collections and emigrant-agent archives. The page says the museum is working to make the archive digitally searchable online and meanwhile asks visitors to get in touch beforehand, tell the museum what they are looking for and arrange access. It also collects new letters and can scan originals a family wishes to keep. The site menu also lists a photograph collection and a library. I did not find an online catalogue on the pages I opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page and archive page on 2026-11-08; the library and photo pages were not opened.

providers.name: Norway Heritage (emigrant ships and passenger lists)
providers.what: Long-running site on Norwegian emigration, recently rebuilt according to its home page. Searchable parts listed there: an emigrant ship database, Atlantic crossings in a chosen date range (currently 1870 to 1905), Norwegian departures year by year for 1825-1925, passenger lists for 1825-1875, a database drawn from a book of Norwegians in America (chapters limited to surnames A to L and S), a book on Norwegian settlements in the United States and Canada, an image gallery, articles, a list of emigration agents and a forum. There is a login link. I did not run searches or test what needs an account.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: DigitaltMuseum (Norway and Sweden museum collections)
providers.what: Shared portal for the digital collections of Norwegian and Swedish museums, with sister domains for each country and an English interface. The home page offers search across content types, a museum list, collection list, map and virtual experiences, and says a free login lets users save searches, follow museums and download search results. In practice the material is mostly photographs and objects, which can carry place names and sometimes named subjects. I did not search or see specific series.
providers.triageNote: Read the Norwegian and Swedish home pages on 2026-11-08; no search run, so no named series seen.

providers.name: Alvin (platform for digital collections and digitised cultural heritage, Sweden)
providers.what: Swedish cross-institution platform for archives, books, manuscripts, images, maps and other objects. providers.triageNote: Read the start page on 2026-11-08; no search was run.

providers.name: SvenskaGravar (Swedish burial search)
providers.what: Search site for people buried in Swedish cemeteries run by cemetery administrations. The page text says users can search by name, cemetery, town, administration and date, with an advanced search, and states it covers 1,155 cemeteries under 143 administrations; the count of buried persons showed as 0 in the unscripted page, so the volume is unconfirmed. providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: Föreningen DIS (Sweden) - Disbyt exchange database
providers.what: Swedish computer-genealogy society, publisher of the Disgen family-tree program. The site also hosts tutorials, a forum and an English mini-site. It is a compiled, user-submitted source, so entries need checking against registers. I did not find how a non-member searches Disbyt.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; the Disbyt access terms and search were not opened.

providers.name: Folkrörelsearkivet i Västerbotten (county archive of popular movements)
providers.what: County archive in Västerbotten for records of local associations and popular movements. providers.triageNote: Read the home page and databases page on 2026-11-08; databases themselves were not opened.

providers.name: Íslendingabók (Icelandic genealogical database)
providers.what: Genealogical database of the inhabitants of Iceland, built by a research company and a software entrepreneur from church records, censuses, resident registers and other sources. providers.name: Héraðsskjalasafn Árnesinga (Árnessýsla Provincial Archives) and Myndasetur
providers.what: Provincial archive for Árnessýsla in south Iceland, in Selfoss. The page lists services including a photograph collection that it scans and publishes, documents from the holdings available on the web, finding aids published online and in the reading room, private archives taken from individuals, societies and firms, and records handed over by local councils. providers.name: DIGAR Eesti artiklid (DEA, Estonian digitised newspapers and periodicals)
providers.what: Estonian portal for digitised newspapers, journals and serials published in Estonian, in Estonia or abroad. The browse list showed 1,772 newspapers, 711 journals and 591 serial publications, and a year picker from 1811 on. The about page says earlier periods are only partly available, publications are added gradually, anyone can browse and search, bibliographic data are always visible and full-text access varies by title, with the newest issues usually not viewable remotely. Full-text and title/author search are offered, in Estonian, English and Russian. A login link exists. I did not search or open an issue.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page and about page on 2026-11-08; no search or issue opened.

providers.name: VAU - Rahvusarhiivi virtuaalne uurimissaal (National Archives of Estonia virtual reading room)
providers.what: Virtual reading room of the National Archives of Estonia, with ordering of files and copies, archive enquiries, a web shop and guidance pages for genealogy, local history, real estate and school history. The genealogy page says family research can be done free of charge in the Saaga portal after registering as a user, that documents not in Saaga are described in the archive information system AIS and consulted in reading rooms, and links to name indexes, a cemetery database, an Estonian manors portal, the place-names database and the Estonian Genealogical Society. Saaga itself already has a row; this row is the service portal around it.
providers.triageNote: Read the VAU front page and its English genealogy page on 2026-11-08; Saaga and AIS were not entered.

providers.name: Luteri koguduste personaalraamatute nimeregister (name index to Lutheran congregations' personal books, Estonia)
providers.what: Name index offered by the National Archives of Estonia for the personal books (personaalraamatud) of Lutheran parishes. The form searches by surname, county and congregation, with a long drop-down of Estonian congregations including Tallinn, Tartu, Pärnu, Narva and many rural parishes, and Valga. I did not run a search, so the years covered, the number of entries and what an entry shows are not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search form on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: KNAB - Eesti Keele Instituudi kohanimeandmebaas (Estonian place names database)
providers.what: Place-names database of the Institute of the Estonian Language, with queries for Estonian place names (46,173 named features as of October 2018), foreign place names (115,270 as of July 2022) and world languages, scripts and peoples (5,600 entries as of 2013). Help pages cover spelling, language codes, sources, status of names and administrative-unit codes. The front page notes that further development is described elsewhere, and the address has moved to an archive host, so the data may be frozen. Useful for locating Estonian villages and farms. I did not run a query.
providers.triageNote: Opened the front page on 2026-11-08 (redirected from eki.ee/knab); no query run; data dates are those printed on the page.

providers.name: Mois.ee (Estonian manors portal)
providers.what: Portal on Estonian manors, which the page says is meant to cover all of them: over 1,245 main manors, 108 pastorates and nearly 600 dairy manors at their peak a century ago. It offers a list, a general section, a map and a detailed search, with articles on manor history. Started in 1999, it is now maintained by the Estonian Academy of Arts with students and volunteers. A manor name is often the key to which parish and estate records cover a family. I opened only the front page.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page on 2026-11-08; no manor entry opened.

providers.name: Ebreji Latvijā 1941-1945 / Jews of Latvia: Names and Fates (University of Latvia)
providers.what: Database run by the Centre for Judaic Studies at the University of Latvia. The front page says it holds the names of 90,244 Jews who lived in Latvia on the eve of the Holocaust and that 59,500 fates have been identified. The site has pages on method, search options, surnames and the sources used, in Latvian, English and Russian, and a search page. The Jewish Museum in Riga also points to it as a source for Jews who lived in Latvia before the war. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page on 2026-11-08 and the museum's 'Roots in Latvia' page that points to it; no search run.

providers.name: LitvakSIG (Lithuanian-Jewish genealogy special interest group)
providers.what: Volunteer research group for Jewish families from the old Lithuanian lands. The site is organised by district research groups (Kaunas, Vilnius, Šiauliai, Panevėžys, Telšiai, Suwałki and others), with special projects such as internal passports and Vilnius household registers, and pages describing archives in Lithuania. Its collective-data page lists files for censuses, craftsmen lists, conscription, emigration, police and arrest lists spanning the 1840s to the 1950s, and says the data sit in a password-protected part open to qualified contributors to the groups. File names are public but records are not. The site has a login.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and the collective-data page on 2026-11-08; the protected data were not seen.

providers.name: Lithuanian Research and Studies Center (Lemont, Illinois)
providers.what: Lithuanian emigre archive and library near Chicago. Its home page claims 300,000 pages of displaced-persons archives from over 130 camps, over 2,500 periodical titles from 1850 onward, over 2,000 boxes of personal, organisational and diplomatic archives and about 100,000 books. The archives page splits the holdings into individuals, organisations, manuscripts and musicology; the library has its own catalogue site. The page does not say what is online. I did not check the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and archives page on 2026-11-08; catalogue not opened.

providers.name: Malta Parish Archives (Hill Museum & Manuscript Library, Malta Study Center)
providers.what: Finding site for Maltese and Gozitan parish records microfilmed by the Malta Study Center between 1980 and 1989, with later digitised additions, under a 2014 agreement with the Archdiocese of Malta. Menu items are parishes (short histories), a catalogue, a map and a lexicon of search terms. The catalogue page says images are viewed in HMML's Reading Room, that registration is free, that images cannot be downloaded and that copies can be requested. I did not enter the Reading Room or check which parishes and years are complete.
providers.triageNote: Read the home, about, parishes and catalogue pages on 2026-11-08; Reading Room not opened.

providers.name: Agjencia Shtetërore e Arkivave të Kosovës (State Agency of Archives of Kosovo)
providers.what: State archive agency in Pristina. The 'what we keep' page says it holds about 9,000 linear metres, nearly 95 million documents from the 15th century to today, in over 1,310 fonds and collections from state bodies, courts, schools, cultural and health bodies and from individuals and families, including material from the diaspora; it also runs a library. A page titled online catalogue and a guide to searching 'SEMMA' exist. The 'search archive material' page says research is done in the reading room under the 2024 archives law and rules. The site has Albanian, English and Serbian versions. I did not test the online catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home, what-we-keep, search-material and online-catalogue pages on 2026-11-08; catalogue search not run.

providers.name: Историјски архив Београда (Historical Archives of Belgrade)
providers.what: City archive of Belgrade. Its fonds and collections pages include a collection of church registers (crkvene matične knjige): 823 books, 1721-1919, in Serbian and Latin, described as first-rank sources of baptisms, marriages and deaths, and noting that keeping registers became compulsory in Serbia around 1837. Other listed holdings include the Belgrade city administration, the Zemun magistrate, municipality fonds and personal and family fonds. The site has a search of fonds and collections, price list and reading-room information. I did not use the search or check access to the registers.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and the church-register collection page on 2026-11-08; fonds search not run.

providers.name: Дигитална БМС (Digital Library of Matica Srpska, Novi Sad)
providers.what: Digital library of the Matica Srpska library in Novi Sad. The menu lists manuscripts, Serbian books from the 15th-17th, 18th and 1801-1867 periods, periodicals and newspapers, calendars and almanacs, small printed matter, journals and collections, postcards, posters, photographs, maps and city plans, and books after 1867. providers.name: Digital Archives Initiative (DAI), Memorial University of Newfoundland / Newfoundland and Labrador digitised newspapers and collections

providers.triageNote: Opened dai.mun.ca/digital (collection list) and the Centre for Newfoundland Studies 'Digitized NL Material' page on 2026-11-08 by page text. No newspaper issue or search opened. Newspaper years are as listed on the page. The page states no access terms.

providers.name: BIFHSGO Name Index (home children, immigration and military indexes), British Isles Family History Society of Greater Ottawa
providers.what: A name index built by volunteers of the Ottawa society, which says one search returns a link to every record with that name from its data sources. The page describes home-child sources: an index of Barnardo's Ups and Downs magazine (Toronto, 1895-1949), the Children's Emigration Homes (Middlemore) index, Fegan Homes 1885-1939 (3,530 names), Father Hudson's photo album and a Home Children 1869-1892 index of more than 14,000 entries taken from Department of Agriculture RG17 records. It also lists military indexes, among them Canadian militia personnel born outside Canada in 1907 (1,991 names), Rideau Canal soldiers and WWI dead at No. 1 Canadian Casualty Clearing Station. The page notes the society works with Library and Archives Canada and that most underlying Middlemore documents are on microfilm elsewhere. I did not run a search or test whether any part of the index needs membership.
providers.triageNote: Opened bifhsgo.ca/name-index on 2026-11-08 and read the source descriptions. Search form not used. Membership requirements not tested.

providers.name: British Home Children Registry, Home Children Canada
providers.what: A registry of children sent from Britain to Canada between 1869 and 1948, kept by the charity Home Children Canada. The registry page showed a running total of 84,220 children and a last-update stamp of 7 November 2026, and says it grew from two earlier private databases that were merged (an initial list of about 61,000 names). The page advises using the 'expand surname' or 'expand name' options because spellings vary. The same organisation's other pages carry notes on where agency records (Barnardo's, Quarrier's, Fegan's, Catholic homes) are held in Britain, with fees for next-of-kin enquiries. I did not run a registry search, so what a result row shows and whether there are limits for non-members are not checked.
providers.triageNote: Opened /registry and /registrylinks on 2026-11-08 (page text). Search not run. Registry count and update date are as displayed that day.

providers.name: Société de généalogie de Québec: bases de données (public and members' databases)
providers.what: The Quebec City genealogical society's page that separates databases open to everyone from those reserved for members. The open list I read includes Archiv-Histo's Ile d'Orleans database, Drummondville-area cemeteries, an index of notarial deeds transcribed by the society, a centenarians list (1713-2016), the Compagnies franches de la Marine, Parisian notarial records on pioneer families, parishes of Canada, surnames and 'dit' names, and a pioneers-by-marriage list (1617-1825). The members' list includes Quebec deaths 1926-1997, Quebec marriages 1926-1997, the Magnan dictionary, justices of the peace (1763-1908), the Soleil obituary index (1999-2004) and Genealogie Quebec/PRDH access. The page says some databases may contain errors. I did not open any individual database.
providers.triageNote: Opened the society's database page on 2026-11-08 (page text, French). Individual databases not opened; what each returns and how a member login works were not tested.

providers.name: The Island Register (Prince Edward Island genealogy, archived)
providers.what: A long-running Prince Edward Island genealogy site online since 1996. Its home page says no further updates will be made after the founder's death in 2021 and that the family is keeping it online as it stands. It lists about 1,164 pioneer family pages, over 4,500 online documents (censuses, directories, church records, maps) and databases for land records, postal records, family Bible records and wills. It also has an index of passenger lists and shipping, a P.E.I. ships database, cemetery pages, obituary books, diaries and a directory of where P.E.I. newspapers are held. Search is by a site search box and category index pages. I did not open the individual databases, so years and completeness are unchecked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Category pages and databases not opened. The site states it is frozen, so material is as of 2021.

providers.name: General Synod Archives, Anglican Church of Canada (with online archives catalogue)
providers.what: The national archives of the Anglican Church of Canada, whose online catalogue lets visitors search by title, fonds, name, place, subject or identifier, filter by year range, and browse fonds, names, places and subjects. Record types in the catalogue include archival descriptions, photographs, books, microforms and periodicals, and there are video databases that can be viewed online. The archives' own page says the reading room in Toronto is open by appointment and that reproductions are subject to a fee schedule. That page says the archives works with Anglican diocesan archives across Canada and links to a list of them, but it does not say that parish registers or diocesan records are held at Toronto. I did not search the catalogue, so I cannot say what genealogical series it holds.
providers.triageNote: Opened archives.anglican.ca (catalogue front page) and anglican.ca/archives on 2026-11-08 (page text). Catalogue search not run; holdings of registers not confirmed.

providers.name: Centre d'etudes acadiennes Anselme-Chiasson (Universite de Moncton)
providers.what: The Acadian studies archive and documentation centre at the Universite de Moncton. Its home page lists an index of parish registers for Cap-Pele and Memramcook, genealogy publications, indexes to the L'Evangeline newspaper photograph collections and a photographic negative collection, institutional and private archives with analytical inventories and digital finding aids, folklore archives, an index of the Moniteur acadien, and French-language newspapers. It gives opening hours for Tuesday to Friday and points to an access and consultation policy and a library catalogue. The page does not describe online databases or give year ranges. A separate search summary I read said the centre holds a microfilm copy of most Maritime Acadian parish registers, which I did not see stated on the page and do not repeat as fact.
providers.triageNote: Opened the centre's home page on 2026-11-08 (page text, French). Finding aids and the catalogue not opened. Wikidata id matched by name.

providers.name: Virtual Museum of Metis History and Culture (Gabriel Dumont Institute)
providers.what: A website of the Gabriel Dumont Institute in Saskatchewan presenting Metis history through collections you can browse and search. The home page lists a biography and essay collection, oral history and traditional stories, an archival collection, an image collection that includes photograph collections from individuals and local centres, art and cultural items, and learning resources. It does not mention scrip records or a genealogy section, so it is a context and photograph source rather than a records index. The page carries a note that videos may not play correctly in some browsers. I did not open any item, and the page does not state terms of use.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Collection pages not opened. Genealogical usefulness untested.

providers.name: Newfoundland's Grand Banks genealogy site (NGB)
providers.what: A non-profit, volunteer-run site, online since 1999 and hosted by Chebucto Community Net, that transcribes Newfoundland records. The home page lists sections for census and lists of inhabitants (fishing rooms and planters), vital statistics, parish records (baptisms, marriages, burials), newspaper obituaries, directories, cemetery transcriptions (with a headstone photo database), passenger lists, wills, petition, jury and voters' lists, colonial office and House of Assembly records, and district pages. Years are not given on the home page. The site asks that material be used for personal purposes only. I did not open individual transcription pages.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). No section opened. Years per section not seen; no price or login statement seen.

providers.name: The Presbyterian Church in Canada Archives
providers.what: The national archives of the Presbyterian Church in Canada. Its home page states holdings of more than 3,500 square feet of textual records, about 30,000 photographs, architectural plans, thousands of hours of audio-visual recordings and well over a million pages of microfilm, with an oldest item from 1638. It mentions congregational records, a thematic guide to residential school records and online finding aids. A research reading room with microfilm readers is described, and researchers are asked to submit a request form because of volume. The page does not say that parish registers or genealogy help are offered, so family-history use is unconfirmed. I did not open the finding aids.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Finding aids and request form not opened.

providers.name: Canadian Letters and Images Project (Vancouver Island University)
providers.what: An online archive of Canadian wartime letters, photographs and audio letters based in the history department of Vancouver Island University, with the Canadian War Museum as a patron. Collections are grouped as Pre-1914, World War One, World War Two, Korea, post-Korea and special items. The home page says a platform upgrade has limited the site, the search feature is not fully working, and each collection is reached through the Collections menu and an alphabetical list. No new collections will be added until the upgrade is done. The site says donations keep content freely available. I did not open a collection list or an individual letter.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Collection pages not opened, so 'free' rests on the site's own statement. Search was reported as limited.

providers.name: Saskatchewan Genealogical Society (SGS): Residents Index, Cemetery Index, Burial Index
providers.what: A registered charity founded in 1969 that runs a lending library and several province-wide indexes. The home page names a Saskatchewan Residents Index (obituaries are included in it since 2002), a Cemetery Index of cemeteries recorded or transcribed by members, and a Burial Index of people buried in Saskatchewan cemeteries and burial sites. The link addresses suggest the Residents Index is for members and the Cemetery Index is public, but the page does not say so in words and shows no year ranges. Memberships run by calendar year. I did not open any index or run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Indexes not opened; the member/public split is inferred from link paths only, hence 'mixed' with a caution.

providers.name: Manitoba Genealogical Society: Manitoba Name Index (MANI) and library
providers.what: The provincial genealogical society's site, whose main database is the Manitoba Name Index, called a member benefit on the home page. A family-name search shows how many MANI records match before joining, and full access needs membership. The page also lists an online library catalogue, a store, research assistance and a Manitoba cemetery transcriptions category. It notes that many records cannot be in the database because of copyright and points to its Resource Library for those. Years covered by MANI are not stated on the page. I did not run a name count or open the cemetery pages.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Search not run. Cemetery transcriptions not opened.

providers.name: New Brunswick Genealogical Society (NBGS) online projects
providers.what: A volunteer-run society founded in 1978 with five regional branches. Its home page lists online projects: an Anglican Registers Project (baptism, marriage and burial records from the 1780s, with name counts of about 1.3 to 1.4 million given in two places), a Probate Records Project from the 1780s, an obituaries index of New Brunswick newspaper notices, a finding aid to genealogical material at the Provincial Archives, and listings of library collections. Cemetery and burial transcriptions are sorted by county, and a province-wide cemetery database is described as planned. The page says members have unlimited access to the online resources and that queries are free, but does not say which pages are open to non-members. I did not open any project.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). No project database opened. Wikidata id matched by name and description.

providers.name: British Columbia Genealogical Society (BCGS): member databases and research centre
providers.what: The province's genealogical society. The home page lists members' resources including BC Cemeteries, a BC Pioneer Registry Index, a clippings index, BC church records and memorials, plus member access to MyHeritage and NewspaperArchive. A Researching in BC page links to the UBC Open Collections BC historical newspapers and BC city directories (1860-1955). The research centre has a catalogue, directories, a vertical file library, indexes and journals, and is open on three days a week. Full membership is stated as 65 dollars. The page does not say whether the library or the public links need membership. I did not open the databases.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Databases not opened; UBC newspaper site is behind an unusual-activity block for scripts and was not read.

providers.name: Alberta Family Histories Society (Calgary): Alberta Ancestors cemetery database and resource centre
providers.what: A Calgary society whose home page describes Alberta Ancestors, a cemetery database with over 240,000 names and almost 170,000 photographs from nearly 300 cemeteries in Calgary and southern Alberta. It also runs a volunteer-staffed resource centre in south Calgary that is open to the public, with a catalogue of books and publications, research assistance, a searching-for-surnames page and special interest groups. The society says it has helped people for more than 40 years. The page does not state which databases are free and which need membership. I did not run a cemetery search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Cemetery search not opened. Counts are as stated on the page.

providers.name: Fichier Origine (origins of French and foreign emigrants settled in Quebec to 1865)
providers.what: A French-language online file on the family origins of pioneers who settled in Quebec up to 1865, owned by the Federation quebecoise des societes de genealogie under a cooperation agreement with the French federation of genealogy. It collects baptism and civil or notarial records found in the home country for married people, single people and nuns. The home page claims over 6,730 entries, among them groups such as the Filles du roi, Montcalm's soldiers and Carignan-Salieres soldiers. A search-help section exists, but the page does not describe the search or say whether access is free. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the French home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Search not used; counts are the site's own.

providers.name: Archiv-Histo (Parchemin notarial records database, Quebec 1626-1809)
providers.what: A research society's site presenting Parchemin, a database of notarial records from old Quebec which the page describes as a nearly complete inventory of notarial deeds from the earliest period to 1809 (coverage starts in 1626). The page offers a search tool for selected deeds and a section on search operators. It states that subscriptions are reserved for institutions and that others should send a request through the contact page. The Quebec City genealogical society also lists an Archiv-Histo database of the Ile d'Orleans among its open databases, which I did not open here. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text, French). Search not used. Subscription terms as stated on the page.

providers.name: Archives de la Ville de Quebec
providers.what: The municipal archives of Quebec City. The page lists about 150 private fonds (including mayors, photographers and collectors and the photographic archive of the newspaper Le Soleil), roughly 300,000 iconographic documents, 200,000 maps and plans, 5,600 microfilms, 2,000 audiovisual items and about 10 linear kilometres of textual records. It links to an online archive search and to a search-and-order service. The page does not give date ranges and does not mention parish or civil registers, so it should be treated as a city-records and images source. I did not open the search or the services page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archives page on 2026-11-08 (page text, French). Online search and ordering pages not opened; consultation-room rules not read.

providers.name: Genealogie acadienne (genealogie-acadienne.net)
providers.what: A French-language genealogy database of Acadian families online since 2008. The home page claims more than 1.1 million individuals and over 200,000 photographs and certificates, with about 200,000 people who died less than a century ago. There is a search page, lists of surnames, families and places, and a 'today in history' feature. A free account can be created and a premium account exists, but the page does not say what is limited to subscribers. It names no operating organisation. I did not search or open any person page, and the site is a compiled tree rather than a primary record index.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text, French). Search not run; operator not identified on the page.

providers.name: Canada GenWeb Cemetery Project
providers.what: A volunteer project, running since 2004, that records Canadian cemeteries and says it offers free searchable access to over 21,000 cemeteries. The home page offers Find a Cemetery, Find a Person and browsing by locality, and adds names, histories, locations, gravestone photographs and transcripts with offers to look up entries. Recent update notices name Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Quebec and Saskatchewan. The page gives no per-province counts and no total of people. I did not run a search, so the free claim is the site's own statement.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Searches not run.

providers.name: Upper Canada Land Petitions index (Ontario Genealogy site)
providers.what: An alphabetical index of Upper Canada land petitions on the Ontario (Upper Canada) Genealogy site. The page states 51,000 records indexed, plus a separate index of land leases and miscellaneous petitions with 10,000 records. Each letter of the alphabet opens its own page, and there is a site search box with an advice to use every known spelling of a family name. It shows four sample images of a typical petition record. The page does not state years or name the source series, so the link to the archival originals is not confirmed here. I did not open a letter page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the index home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Letter pages not opened; source series and years not stated on the page.

providers.name: CanadianObits.com
providers.what: A family-research site that collects obituaries, death notices, memorials and funeral notices from across Canada, with a page for each province. Content comes from funeral home records, newspaper records and contributed submissions. The home page also links a free obituary index on a newspaper archive site (marked as possibly needing a subscription for some data), a search-by-name form, a Canadian notables index for 1999-2000 and surname origin pages. No date range is given for the site's own collection. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Province pages not opened.

providers.name: Societe des Filles du roi et soldats du Carignan (SFRSC)
providers.what: A non-profit heritage association for descendants and researchers of the Filles du roi and Carignan-Salieres soldiers of 17th century New France. The site carries pages on both groups, a New France by the Numbers page, sample journal articles and a research resources page with links for French-Canadian ancestry. Full membership is for documented descendants and associate membership for others. Some content is public and some appears to sit behind a member login, but fees are not shown. I did not open a list of people or any article.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Individual pages and the research resources page not opened.

providers.name: JewishGen Canada Database
providers.what: A search form on JewishGen for records of individuals living in Canada, drawn from several sources, with nearly 250,000 entries combined and new entries added regularly. The search chooses a data type (surname, given name, town or any field) and a match type from exact through phonetic to fuzzy, with an optional region filter. When I opened it the list of component databases failed to load, so I could not see the record sets or years. The page says a multi-criteria search is for donors giving 180 dollars or more to the JewishGen General Fund. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Component database list did not load; no search run.

providers.name: Mennonite Archives of Ontario (Conrad Grebel University College)
providers.what: The archives of Ontario Mennonites, cared for by Conrad Grebel University College in the Milton Good Library at Waterloo. It collects materials on religious, congregational, family and personal life. The site lists History Online (digitised collections), a search of the archives with documents, photographs, genealogy resources and research guides, and says nineteenth and early twentieth century church records of Ontario Mennonite clergy and congregations are being digitised on a vital records page as staff time allows. Staff answer genealogy questions that take about fifteen minutes or less, and detailed research needs a visit; copies are requested through the contact page. I did not open the vital records page (a guess at its address returned not found).
providers.triageNote: Opened the archives' home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Vital records and search pages not opened. Visit fees not read.

providers.name: Loyalist Collection, University of New Brunswick Libraries
providers.what: A special collection on the fifth floor of the Harriet Irving Library in Fredericton holding British and colonial North American primary sources, mainly from about 1750 to 1850. Its focus is American Revolutionary War Loyalists, but it also covers the wider British Atlantic world including the British West Indies. Most items are on microfilm, some are in other microformats and a limited number are digital. A catalogue can be searched or browsed for item descriptions. The page says the collection is for in-person, self-service use during library hours and that appointments are needed for staff help. It does not name individual series such as muster rolls or petitions, and I did not open the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Opened loyalist.lib.unb.ca on 2026-11-08 (page text) and the UNB Archives and Special Collections page. Catalogue not opened.

providers.name: New Brunswick Museum: Archives and Research Library (Saint John)
providers.what: The archives and research library of the provincial museum in Saint John. The page describes about 1,000 metres of personal papers, business and institutional records and ephemera on the province's economic, legal, military, religious, cultural, social and political life, with an emphasis on the 19th century and a few items older. It adds nearly 50,000 photographs from the 1840s onward and a research library of about 100,000 books and 500 periodical titles, including the Webster, Ganong and Odell libraries. Three catalogues are linked, for archives, photographs and the library. The museum's home page says it hopes to reopen in 2028, so check availability before a visit. The page does not describe access rules, and I did not open the catalogues.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archives page and the museum home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Catalogues not opened. Closure/reopening note comes from the museum home page.

providers.name: Black Loyalist Heritage Centre (Nova Scotia)
providers.what: A heritage centre on the Black Loyalist settlement history of the 1780s. The home page describes an interactive display where visitors can search more than 3,000 listings for names of original Black Loyalists (the Book of Negroes), an invitation to search for ancestral roots inside the centre, and a link to Black Loyalist digital collections. The page does not say whether the name search can be used online or only on site. It gives opening hours on weekdays and admission prices. I did not open the digital collections, and the page does not describe research services.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Digital collections not opened; online availability of the name search unknown.

providers.name: National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation (NCTR) archives
providers.what: The archive of material gathered by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada on the Indian residential school system, hosted at the University of Manitoba. The site's menu lists an Archives and Collections section with an overview, a public database, how to access records, survivor and family requests, legislation and licensing and an interactive map. I read only the home page and menu, so I cannot say what the public database contains or what proof is needed to request records. Sections also cover education resources and exhibits. The site carries a residential school crisis line number, and the material is sensitive.
providers.triageNote: Opened nctr.ca home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). The public database page returned an image rather than text through the fetch tool and was not read.

providers.name: PRDH-IGD: Programme de recherche en demographie historique (Quebec population register before 1860)
providers.what: A site of the historical demography research programme that describes itself as the comprehensive site for French-Canadian genealogy of Quebec before 1860. Its text tagline is all that came through when I opened the home page, because the pages run on scripts. The programme's name suggests a population register built from parish records, but I did not see the record types, years covered, search method or cost stated, so those are unchecked. The Quebec City genealogical society lists access to Genealogie Quebec/PRDH among its member databases. A later pass with a normal browser should open the search pages.
providers.triageNote: Opened prdh-igd.com on 2026-11-08; only the tagline rendered through the fetch tool. English page and search not seen. Row is thin on purpose.

providers.name: Bermuda National Library: Bermudiana Collection and digital newspapers
providers.what: The national library of Bermuda in Hamilton. Its Bermudiana Collection page gives newspaper holdings with run dates: Royal Gazette from 1784, Bermuda Sun from 1964, Mid-Ocean News 1961 to 2009, Bermuda Times 1987-1995 and The Recorder 1933-1975, with older papers on microfilm and current copies in the reading room. A Bermuda Index covers local newspapers and most magazines from about 1958 to 2000. A digital newspaper collection is stated to include the Royal Gazette 1784-1899 and the Bermuda Recorder July 1933 to July 1975, made from the library's microfilm. Most Bermuda items are in a closed collection that needs a request form and at least 24 hours, with a fee for off-site retrieval. The page mentions a genealogy guide and a local studies enquiry line. I did not open the digital collection.
providers.triageNote: Opened bnl.bm home page and the Bermudiana Collection page on 2026-11-08 (page text). The link to the digital collection was not on the page text and was not opened.

providers.name: Barbados Museum and Historical Society: library and genealogy research services
providers.what: The research library of the Barbados museum, with over 7,000 monographs, journals and pamphlets on Barbadian and Caribbean history, a rare-book collection of 17th to 19th century imprints, the Shilstone Notebooks and documents such as the Lascelles Slavery Archive. The page says some rare books are digitised and that a historical and genealogical database is offered to remote users. A Research Services page describes comprehensive genealogy services and custom research, with enquiries through the contact form. Neither page gives fees or visiting rules, and the online collections address mentioned on the library page refused automated access (403). I did not see what the genealogical database contains.
providers.triageNote: Opened the library and research services pages on 2026-11-08 (page text). The Online Collections site returned 403 to scripts and was not read; the Genealogy page address I tried was not found.

providers.name: Caribbean Genealogy Library (St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands)
providers.what: A volunteer-run, member-supported library in St. Thomas for Virgin Islands and wider Caribbean family history, with over 5,000 books, periodicals and microfilms and a Family History Library affiliate status. Its online resources page links finding aids to Danish West Indies passenger records (arrival and departure registers for St. Thomas and Christiansted, 1794-1899, digitised by the Danish archives), a list of Danish West Indies documents of interest, a St. Thomas and St. John cemetery and death database of over 25,000 records that is queried through the library, and an indexed collection of almost 4,000 Virgin Islands funeral booklets. A links page points to Danish, Dutch, French and British Caribbean archives. The library is open three days a week and by appointment. I did not use the finding aids.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home, visit, online resources, passenger, Maria Smith cemetery, funeral booklet, Rigsarkivet and links pages on 2026-11-08 (page text). No finding aid opened; I did not copy any names.

providers.name: Rigsarkivet: finding people in the Danish West Indies (research guide)
providers.what: A research guide from the Danish National Archives for the former Danish West Indies, now the U.S. Virgin Islands, organised by group: enslaved people and labourers, free people of colour, European civilians and military. It lists censuses between 1835 and 1911, parish registers from 1691 to 1920 (Evangelical, Black Lutheran Mission and Dutch Reformed), congregation reports from 1805 to 1918, slave lists from 1772 to 1821, lists of free coloured persons from 1744 to 1831, military rolls and service records, and two name indexes. The guide advises knowing an island, town or plantation and religious community. It links to digitised records but does not state costs. I did not follow the links into the image viewer.
providers.triageNote: Opened the guide page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Digitised record links not opened; crowdsourcing site cs.rigsarkivet.dk reset the connection and was not read.

providers.name: Coleccion Aruba (digital heritage collection, with the Database of People Enslaved on Aruba 1840-1863)
providers.what: The shared digital collection of Aruba's national library, national archives and partners, in Papiamento, Dutch and English. The home page lists browse options for texts, images, video and audio and a list of Aruban newspapers and periodicals. A project page describes a database of people enslaved on Aruba between 1840 and 1863, drawn from the slavery registers and shown as family trees, built by the national archives, the national library and a cultural partner. Content is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 according to that page. A search summary also mentioned civil registration indexes on WieWasWie, which I did not verify. I did not open the register trees beyond one page and copied no names.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and one tree page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Search and the full database not tested. National Archives of Aruba Wikidata item is Q17082115 but this is the shared collection, so left null.

providers.name: Jamaican Family Search
providers.what: A privately run virtual genealogy library for Jamaica, aimed at people with ancestors before 1920, holding about 297,000 names. The home page lists almanacs from 1751 to 1877, directories from 1878 to 1910, Church of England, Catholic, Wesleyan, Moravian and Jewish registers, over 450 transcribed wills with a Supreme Court will index (1725-1930), land grants 1735-1824, immigrant lists for 1840-1841, French refugee lists of 1795, a 1823 Hanover census and 1831 Maroon returns. Search uses a site search box, and the page advises trying spelling variants and browsing the site index. It does not state a price, and part of the content sits under member pages. Use is limited to personal non-commercial purposes.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). No database page opened; which parts need membership was not tested.

providers.name: Jamaican Ancestral Records: index of tombstone records in Jamaica
providers.what: A site that describes itself as an index of tombstone records taken in Jamaica. The pages are arranged by parish (Clarendon, Hanover, Kingston, Manchester, Portland, St Andrew, St Ann, St Catherine, St Elizabeth, St James, St Mary, St Thomas, Trelawny, Westmoreland) and include military burials such as the Garrison and Briggs Park, and naval burials. The page has a search box with no instructions, no date range, no stated cost, and does not identify who runs it. It is hosted on a general blogging platform. I did not open a parish page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (page text). Parish pages not opened; operator not identified.

providers.name: Index to early wills of Jamaica, 1655-1816 (JamWorld Genealogy)
providers.what: An index of 7,823 Jamaican wills from 1655 to 1816 split into four alphabetical pages (surnames A-D, E-L, M-R, S-Z). It draws on Prerogative Court of Canterbury will listings printed in Caribbeana and on lists of wills recorded in Jamaica for 1662-1750 compiled from a British Library manuscript. Each entry gives the testator, a volume name, quire or folio number and year, and the page warns that some wills were recopied under new volume and folio numbers. It tells users to find the will text at the National Archives at Kew, on FamilySearch microfilm or through a researcher in Jamaica. I did not open the alphabetical pages.

The collection is a few dozen files by the facet counts, so it is useful for a specific hunt rather than a general register. I did not determine its date range or open any images.
providers.triageNote: Opened on 2026-11-08 (site and AtoM instances answer normally to a plain fetch).

providers.name: Archivo Nacional de Asunción: Sección Historia (online catalogue)
providers.what: AtoM catalogue of the archive's oldest section, with about 4,380 descriptions when I looked. The archive describes the section as colonial and first-republic administrative papers, council (cabildo) minutes, and official and private correspondence. The creator facet shows many items attributed to the national government of the mid-nineteenth century. The digitisation came from a church-sponsored filming agreement and was later indexed and published online with Iberarchivos support, according to the archive's holdings page. I did not open images or test name searches.
providers.triageNote: Opened on 2026-11-08 (site and AtoM instances answer normally to a plain fetch).

providers.name: Archivo Nacional de Asunción: Sección Nueva Encuadernación (online catalogue)
providers.what: AtoM catalogue of a mixed run of 3,417 bound volumes of administrative papers, correspondence, censuses and some notarial documents from the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries, according to the archive's holdings page. The online facets I saw list governors, the council of Asunción and individual notaries as creators. It is the section where population lists and some deeds are likely to turn up, but the archive itself calls its arrangement of the volumes uneven. I did not open any images.
providers.triageNote: Opened on 2026-11-08 (site and AtoM instances answer normally to a plain fetch).

providers.name: Archivo Nacional Histórico de Chile (ANH)
providers.what: The historical branch of Chile's National Archive in Santiago. Its page lists Spanish colonial administration, nineteenth-century state papers, a map collection of the 17th-19th centuries, court files from the seventeenth century to the early twentieth, and donated or purchased private papers. The site's 'consultar documentos' page says users may search online catalogues, guides to fonds and fonds tables, or use inventories and databases in the reading room, and that the archive also holds judicial, notarial and conservator-of-property records for the whole country. A 2026 synoptic table of fonds is linked from the page. I did not run a catalogue search.
providers.triageNote: Read the ANH page and the 'explora el archivo' page on 2026-11-08. Existing rows cover the archive's home and two named online catalogues.

providers.name: Archivo Regional de La Araucanía (ARA)
providers.what: Regional branch of the national archive in Temuco, open to the public since 1997. Its page says the holdings span 1858-2013 and include notarial protocols and property-registry (conservador de bienes raíces) records for Malleco from 1870 and Cautín from 1887, court files, and regional-government papers. It also holds notarial instruments from the former departments of Angol, Collipulli, Traiguén, Victoria, Lautaro, Temuco, Nueva Imperial and Pitrufquén. A synoptic table of fonds dated 1 February 2026 is referenced. Useful for land and settlement records of the Mapuche frontier and the German, Swiss and Italian colonist era; I did not open the table or any catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the regional page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the fonds table.

providers.name: Archivo Regional de Tarapacá (ART)
providers.what: Regional branch of the Chilean national archive serving the Arica y Parinacota and Tarapacá regions, created in 2001. Its page says the holdings run from 1860 to 2007 and include notarial protocols, property-registry records, court files and regional-government resolutions, plus papers of the agriculture ministry, the environmental service and the old mining service with documents and plans dated 1860-1950. A synoptic table of fonds from 2019 is referenced. For the nitrate-era north, with its Peruvian, Bolivian, Chilean and immigrant populations, the notarial and court material is the likely entry point; I did not open the table or test any search.
providers.triageNote: Read the regional page on 2026-11-08. Address and catalogue not read.

providers.name: Cementerio General de Santiago: Buscador de Sepultados (burial search)
providers.what: Online burial search run by the Cementerio General (Recoleta) in Santiago, Chile's main historic cemetery. The page explains that two series are searchable: family, social and remains plots with records available from 1986, and adult wall niches from 1931 onward, and that earlier years are being added gradually. The form takes first and second given names and paternal and maternal surnames and updates as letters are typed, with a two-letter minimum. I did not run a search, so I cannot say what fields a result shows. Burials before 1931 are not in the search according to the page.
providers.triageNote: Read the page text on 2026-11-08; no query was submitted. Wikidata id is for the cemetery.

providers.name: Historia Política (Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de Chile)
providers.what: Reference site of Chile's congressional library on political history from 1810. Its home page offers biographical profiles of senators and deputies from 1811 to the present, which the site says include family, academic and career information; the verbatim sessions of both chambers from 1811; the constitutions; and interviews with former members. The family detail in the profiles can help place a politician's parents, marriage and descendants. It covers only people who sat in Congress. I read the front page and did not open a profile or test the search.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page on 2026-11-08. No profile opened.

providers.name: Genealogía Familiar (Argentine family-tree database)
providers.what: Free, volunteer-run family-tree database for Argentina, built on research by Argentine genealogists. The site states it began with the founding families of the colonial era and the independence generation. Its statistics page showed about 581 thousand individuals, 207 thousand families, 216 thousand distinct surnames, some 1,800 sources, and tens of thousands of photographs, plus a smaller set of documents and headstone pictures. Tools include surname and name search, advanced search, a relationship finder between two people, a source and repository list, places and cemeteries. Records are compiled trees, not original registers, so each link needs checking against the cited sources. Living people appear in the counts, so treat recent generations with care.
providers.triageNote: Opened the front page and statistics page on 2026-11-08 without logging in. No individual record opened.

providers.name: CEMLA Biblioteca (library of the Latin American Migration Studies Centre)
providers.what: Library of the Centro de Estudios Migratorios Latinoamericanos in Buenos Aires, which the centre describes as the first library devoted only to Argentine migration, with over four thousand volumes of books and serials. It is consulted by appointment, with an e-mail contact on the page. The centre's site also links a list of migration centres, scalabrinian missions and emigration museums in several countries, and the front page advertises the passenger-arrivals database (up to 1960) whose search form is already catalogued under the existing CEMLA row. No online catalogue of the library was seen.
providers.triageNote: Read the library page and the links page on 2026-11-08. The arrivals search is a separate address already in the Atlas.

providers.name: Archivo General de la Provincia de Entre Ríos
providers.what: Provincial archive of Entre Ríos, in Paraná, traced to a government archive created by decree in 1860 and legally established in 1880. It works from two sites: the administrative and historical archive (treasury, education, decrees and court files) and the Archivo Histórico Guillermo Saraví (government fonds, library, legislature papers and newspaper collection). The page says microfilming of several series of the government fonds was done and digitisation added, and the archive offers a virtual tour, a photo gallery and a decrees search. Entre Ríos was a main area of Volga German, Swiss and other colonist settlement, so land and government series are a lead. I did not see a finding aid or learn which series are digitised.
providers.triageNote: Read the archive page and the section page on 2026-11-08. Decrees-search link not followed.

providers.name: Biblioteca Nacional de Uruguay: Colecciones Digitales (BNU-CD)
providers.what: Digital repository of Uruguay's national library. A page on the library's main site says that since 2021 it has been digitising nineteenth and early twentieth century newspapers from the interior departments in partnership with the departmental governments, for issues published up to 1953. The recent-additions list included foreign-community bulletins of the 1920s and 1940s as well as neighbourhood papers. I opened the collections list but no item, so I cannot say how legible the page images are or what the download terms are.

providers.name: Anáforas (digital library of Uruguayan authors and periodicals)

The section's own introduction says it includes publications run by exiles and immigrants, in Italian, French, Portuguese, English and other languages, and gives the date range of each title in the index. For a family historian this is a way to read a community or union paper where an immigrant ancestor may have written or been mentioned. Run as a teaching project, so coverage is uneven; I did not open an issue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page, the project history page and the periodicals section introduction on 2026-11-08. No issue opened.

providers.name: Archivo de Bogotá (Bogotá city historical archive)

It also keeps a bibliographic and newspaper collection and a reading room, and points to its information system, called El Cofre, for searching. A published guide to the fonds is linked. providers.name: Chevra Kadisha de São Paulo (Jewish cemeteries: Butantã, Embu, Vila Mariana, Cubatão)
providers.what: Burial society that runs the Jewish cemeteries of São Paulo state. providers.name: Crew List Index Project (CLIP)
providers.what: A not-for-profit volunteer project that builds finding aids for the records of British merchant seafarers and ships, mainly 1863 to 1913. The site explains that the crew documents themselves have no official index, so CLIP assembles linked indexes: seafarer names transcribed from crew lists, ship data by official number (the pages mention all registered ships from 1855 into the 1950s) and indexed images of the Mercantile Navy List. Pages are grouped as People, Ships and Documents, with notes on sources and limits for each data set, plus guides on what crew lists are and where the originals are held. It also links to other maritime record sites. The site states that it does not carry out paid research. I did not run a name search or open any result.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the CLIP data page on 2026-11-08 and read the descriptions; ran no searches and opened no records.

providers.name: 1915 Crew Lists of the British Merchant Navy (Royal Museums Greenwich)
providers.what: A searchable database of the surviving 1915 crew agreements of British merchant ships, produced by the National Archives and the National Maritime Museum with volunteer transcribers. The site says it holds over 39,000 crew lists with more than 750,000 names, and calls the search free. It explains that a crew agreement was a contract listing each person with rank or rating, address, pay and dates of joining and leaving, and that women and non-British crew appear as well. A short FAQ explains ranks and why a name can appear more than once. The page also credits the Crew List Index Project for technical help. I did not run a search, so what each result shows (and whether page images open) is unchecked; a notice on the page said the site could be offline for maintenance.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and About page on 2026-11-08; no searches run.

providers.name: WhalingHistory.org (whaling voyages and crew lists databases)
providers.what: A data site on the whaling industry that combines logbooks, journals, ship registers, newspapers and customs records. The home page lists American Offshore Whaling Voyages, the British Southern Whale Fishery, British North American, French, Scottish and Australian whaling voyages, and says the data link out to crew lists, digitised logbooks and scans. The text states that there are nine related databases, including one of crew lists for American voyages, and that each entity record has a stable identifier that can be cited. One search box searches all the databases and pages and returns results in separate tabs, and each database has a table-style data viewer. The site has a Crew Lists FAQ explaining where crew lists come from and what they contain. I did not run a search or open a data viewer.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the descriptions; no search run, data viewers not opened.

providers.name: Mystic Seaport Museum: Collections and Research (genealogy databases)
providers.what: The research site of Mystic Seaport Museum's collections centre, which says it keeps maritime art, tools, documents, photographs, about 1,000 ship registers and hundreds of oral history interviews. The Databases page lists crew lists for Salem (1799-1879), New London (1803-1878), Fall River whaling and the whaleship Charles W. Morgan, a Connecticut Ship Database (1789-1939), registers of Seamen's Protection Certificates, and the San Francisco Shanghaiers database for 1886-1890. I opened the Protection Certificates page, which is a sortable table with columns for age, birthplace, customs district, certificate number, date and physical description, with a note that the entries are volunteers' transcriptions kept as written so exact-name matching is unreliable. Other pages list indexes to ship registers and yacht registers and an exhibit on immigration and steamships. I did not test image links.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home, Databases, Indexes and Protection Certificates pages on 2026-11-08; searches not run.

providers.name: Scottish National War Memorial: Roll of Honour search
providers.what: The Scottish National War Memorial sits within Edinburgh Castle and is Scotland's place of remembrance from the First World War onward. Its roll search page says the trustees keep a Roll of Honour for Scots covering both World Wars and conflict deaths since 1945, held in a master database that is copied to the search page from time to time, and that the same content fills the printed books in the Hall of Honour. A search needs at least one of surname, service number or year of death, with options for exact or partial surname match, forename, a date of death and a choice of conflict era. The page says certificates and extracts of a roll entry can be bought. I did not run a search or see a result page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and roll search form on 2026-11-08; did not submit a search.

providers.name: Canadian Great War Project
providers.what: A collaborative database of people who served in the Canadian Expeditionary Force in the First World War, now hosted by the University of Victoria library. The home page says it holds records of 648,362 people. The About page explains that it relies on the documents of Library and Archives Canada and other government agencies, and that members transcribed attestation papers, war diaries and other primary sources and normalised the data fields; members also added letters and images. The site has Search, About and an Engagements section, and needs JavaScript. I did not run a search, so the fields shown and the extent of free access are unchecked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home and About pages on 2026-11-08; the search page was not run.

providers.name: Irish War Memorials (inventory of war memorials in Ireland)

The site says it lists names of people recorded on memorials as well as the memorials themselves, with photographs, and explains how to find and visit a memorial, how to contribute, and what has been added since a previous visit. A help page on finding out more about someone named on a memorial points to a Useful Links list and says the project office holds books on casualties of counties, towns, schools, colleges and workplaces and will search them on request. providers.name: Naval-History.Net (naval casualty lists and records)
providers.what: A volunteer-built reference site on naval history from 1815 onward whose family-history pages carry casualty lists. The First World War page also holds introductions to the French, Greek, Italian, Russian and United States navies, flag officer lists, and a section of those who served. The site is dedicated to its creator's relatives. I did not open the casualty lists themselves or search them.

providers.name: Friends Historical Library, Swarthmore College (Quaker records)
