providers.triageNote: Opened the German home page, the English information page and the English online-search page on 2026-11-08. Did not submit a search; the separate museum family-research page is already an Atlas row (dah-bremerhaven-familienforschung).

providers.name: GEDBAS - Genealogische Datenbank (Verein für Computergenealogie)
providers.what: GEDBAS is a family-tree database on the network of the German computer-genealogy association; the page offers a registration for new accounts alongside the search. The front page offers a new-search form with family name, first name, place name and a time limit, plus statistics pages listing last names and places. Trees are compiled by individual researchers, so entries are leads to be checked against registers rather than records. I did not open a result page, so I cannot say how much of each tree is shown to anonymous visitors.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08 (no challenge, no login needed to see the form). Results and tree pages not opened. Sits beside the existing row compgen-des (the data-entry system) on the same association's network.

providers.name: GOV - Geschichtliches Orts-Verzeichnis (historical gazetteer of places, parishes and administrative units)
providers.what: A volunteer-built gazetteer that gives each place its coordinates, postal and municipal codes, earlier and other names, and its changing administrative and church affiliation over time. The home page says it holds about 1.2 million entries (as of November 2024) covering places, churches, church districts, districts and regions, with emphasis on Europe, North America and Australia. It is aimed at family researchers who need to know which parish or district a place belonged to when a record was made. The search box takes a place name and there is an advanced search. I did not test a search or check the depth for any one region.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; read the project description and the entry count. No search run.

providers.name: Datenbank Historischer Adressbücher (CompGen address-book database)
providers.what: A volunteer project of the computer-genealogy association that makes historical address books, residents' registers and citizens' registers searchable by name. The search form takes family name, given name, occupation, place (via the GOV identifier), address and company name. The front page lists newly added books, which on the day I looked included directories for Schwäbisch Hall, Weinheim, Wanne, Tübingen and others from the 1890s to 1938, and a list of books currently being keyed with a call for helpers. Each book is a separate directory for one town or district, so coverage is patchy and depends on what volunteers have entered. I did not run a search or open a book viewer.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the search fields and the new-books list. No search run; scan viewing not tested.

providers.name: Grabsteine - Friedhofsdatenbank (genealogy.net)
providers.what: A volunteer project recording gravestones and cemeteries, run on the computer-genealogy association's network. The home page counts 10,264 cemeteries in the database and 9 more being recorded, and says all data are freely accessible. Cemeteries can be listed by federal state, by postal code, by Jewish communities outside Germany, by society that recorded them and by newest additions, and shown on a map. There are further pages for notable graves and links. Some of the page text looks old (it carries maintenance notices from 2018 and 2020), so I did not judge how current the counts are, and I did not open an individual cemetery.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; read the counts and the list options. No cemetery page opened.

providers.name: Online-OFBs - Ortsfamilienbücher online (genealogy.net)
providers.what: A catalogue of online local family books, which are family-by-family compilations made from the parish registers of one place. The page lists the available books alphabetically by present-day federal state, starting with a general section (a foundation list, Jews in the former German Reich, Sinti and Roma in the former Reich) and then Baden-Wuerttemberg villages such as Affental, Altsteusslingen, Buchen (Odenwald) and Dettingen unter Teck. It also has statistics, the newest books, the participating societies and a map of available databases. Volunteers who have keyed a church book can submit it. I did not open a book or run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08 at this address, which loaded normally with no challenge. Round 1 recorded online-ofb.de as bot-gated; I did not use that address and did not try to get round it. Search not tested.

providers.name: digiPress - Zeitungsportal der Bayerischen Staatsbibliothek
providers.what: The newspaper portal of the Bavarian State Library, offering mainly German-language historical papers as page scans with full-text search. The home page counts 8,901,490 digitised pages from 866 newspaper companies, 1,307 titles and 1,389,937 issues. Entry points are a title list, a calendar view and a full-text search; the news section mentions additions such as Regensburg official gazettes and 1848/49 revolution papers, and a Mirador-based viewer. Family historians use such papers for notices of births, marriages and deaths and local reports. I did not run a search or open an issue, so the access terms are unconfirmed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the statistics and news; search and viewer not tested.

providers.name: Alemannia Judaica - Arbeitsgemeinschaft zur Erforschung der Geschichte der Juden im süddeutschen Raum
providers.what: A long-running website of a working group on the history of Jews in southern Germany and neighbouring areas. The entry page offers sections on Jewish cemeteries (former and existing), synagogues, an overview of Jewish cultural monuments by region, existing Jewish communities, Jewish museums, research projects, literature and press articles, an address list and links. The sections on communities, synagogues and cemeteries are the likely parts for tracing where a family lived and was buried. The page itself says most search engines index the site well and advises searching it that way. I did not open individual community or cemetery pages or check how far the content has been updated.
providers.triageNote: Opened the entry page on 2026-11-08 and read the section list. Subpages not opened.

providers.name: Stolpersteine Hamburg - Biografien-Datenbank
providers.what: A biography database for the memorial stones set in Hamburg pavements for people persecuted under National Socialism. The new site (announced in early November 2026) says the biographies make visible the people behind the stones and that several thousand stones lie in Hamburg. Each short biography runs from birth year through the path of persecution, often to violent death. There is a search box for stones, a news section and an events list. I did not open a biography or test the search, and I can not say how the new site's coverage compares with the old one.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; read the introduction. Search and biography pages not opened.

providers.name: Stolpersteine in Berlin - gemeinsame Seite der Berliner Initiativen
providers.what: The shared website of the Berlin Stolpersteine initiatives, which describe the project and give information on the stones laid in Berlin since 1996. The start page explains that stones are set at the last freely chosen residence of people persecuted 1933 to 1945, and names the groups now commemorated: Jews, Sinti and Roma, political and religious resistance, homosexual people, Jehovah's Witnesses, victims of the euthanasia murders and people persecuted as supposedly anti-social. It lists local walks and events. I did not open the stone or biography listings, so I do not know how searchable they are by name or street.
providers.triageNote: Opened the start page on 2026-11-08; subpages and search not opened.

providers.name: Staatsarchiv Hamburg (State Archives of Hamburg) - Familienforschung und Namensverzeichnisse
providers.what: The state and city archive of Hamburg, with an online archive database and a family-research section. Its research page links digitised name registers for several series: church-book general registers 1816 to 1866, civil-registration supervision, registry-office books, aliens and passport protocols from the registration office, and naturalisation files. The page on civil registers says Hamburg registry books are held for births from 1874/1876 to 1915, marriages to 1945 and deaths to 1995, and that the books to 1901 (births), 1920 (marriages) and 1950 (deaths) were digitised by Ancestry, free in the reading room and paid at home. The general-register page lists the alphabetical church-book indexes in volumes by surname range. I did not search the archive database.
providers.triageNote: Opened the research page, the family-research page, the civil-register page and the general-register page on 2026-11-08. The archive database (actapro) was not searched. No existing Atlas row for this archive.

providers.name: Staatsarchiv Bremen (State Archive of Bremen) - Familienforschung und Personenstandsregister online
providers.what: The state archive of the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen. Its family-research page states that the whole civil-status holdings (series 4.60/5 Personenstand, 4.60/3 Zivilstand and 4.60/7 Stammtafeln), about 1,000,000 scans in 4,570 units, are online in its Arcinsys database, giving continuous Bremen births, marriages and deaths from 1811 to 1914, 1944 or 1994 depending on type, free, without registration, at any hour. A crowdsourced name database made with the Bremen family-history society 'Die Maus' links into those scans. Written genealogical enquiries answered by staff cost a fee. A separate page explains access to the NSDAP membership card file digitised by the US National Archives. I did not open Arcinsys or a register image.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page, the family-research page and the NSDAP card-file page on 2026-11-08; the free-access statement is the archive's own. Arcinsys images and the Maus database were not opened.

providers.name: Sächsisches Staatsarchiv (Saxon State Archives) - Archivgut online
providers.what: The Saxon State Archives publish digitised holdings through an online archive information system. The 'Archivgut online' page, dated 13 October 2026, gives a total of 28,758,845 digitised pages in 153 holdings, listed by archive location, with a link on each holding signature into the finding aid. Digitised items appear on the record in a holding and can be downloaded one image at a time; higher resolution and bulk downloads go through the archive. The page says that frequently used holdings are the ones digitised. This row is the archive as a whole; the existing Atlas row on this host is only the Freiberg mining-archive library. I did not open a holding, so I cannot say which series are church or civil registers, and I did not check whether any login is needed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the 'Archivgut online' page and the home page on 2026-11-08. The existing row de-bibliothek-des-saechsischen-staatsarchivs... covers only the Freiberg library; this is the archive as a whole.

providers.name: Landesarchiv Schleswig-Holstein (State Archives of Schleswig-Holstein) - Online-Recherche mit Arcinsys
providers.what: The state archives of Schleswig-Holstein, at Schleswig. Its web pages explain that the holdings can be searched online in the state's Arcinsys installation (arcinsys.schleswig-holstein.de) by keyword or by browsing the holdings structure, without logging in from anywhere. The page warns that the list is not complete, since items not yet described, or restricted for privacy or archive-law reasons, are not shown, and invites enquiries. An account allows a personal list and requests for reading-room orders. The home page lists news, events and a virtual tour. I did not open Arcinsys or see which holdings (church records, civil registers, estate papers) are described there.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archive's page and the 'Online-Recherche' page on 2026-11-08. Arcinsys itself not opened.

providers.name: Arcinsys Niedersachsen und Bremen - Archivinformationssystem
providers.what: The shared archive information system of the Lower Saxony State Archives, the Bremen State Archive and other Lower Saxon and Bremen archives, developed together with Hesse and Schleswig-Holstein. The start page says that without logging in a visitor can find file titles, charter summaries and information on holdings, view digitised items, and look up archives' contact details and holdings. A free registration adds a personal list, requests to use records, and ordering for the reading room. For family historians it is the route into the Bremen civil-status scans and Lower Saxon holdings. I did not run a search or open an image.
providers.triageNote: Opened the start page on 2026-11-08 and read the stated functions. The Hesse installation (arcinsys.hessen.de) only showed a loading screen to my fetch, so I did not read it.

providers.name: Historisches Archiv der Stadt Köln - Digitaler Lesesaal (DHAK)
providers.what: The virtual reading room of the Cologne city archive, where holdings and single records can be searched by archive structure or across all fields. The page says images of records are shown where they exist and no copyright or protection period prevents it, and that registration is not needed. It notes that civil-status registers and second copies of registry books are under the North Rhine-Westphalia state archive's holdings, with a list of which registry office covered which Cologne district. Items affected by the archive's building collapse are marked so users can see whether a piece is usable again. Orders cannot be made in the reading room and go by e-mail. The page separates the Rhenish Picture Archive, which has its own portal. I did not search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the virtual reading room front page on 2026-11-08; did not search or open a record.

providers.name: MARCHIVUM, Mannheim (city archive) - Recherche, Jüdischer Friedhof, Druckschriften digital
providers.what: The archive, documentation centre and library of the city of Mannheim. Its research page lists online databases: the virtual reading room for archive holdings (replacing an older Findstar/Scope database at the new year), 'Druckschriften Digital' for digitised periodicals such as newspapers, a library catalogue, a chronology of the city, and a database of graves in Mannheim's Jewish cemetery covering 1842 to 2008. The cemetery page explains that the old Jewish cemetery in the town centre was cleared in 1938 and its dead moved to a collective grave, and that the database lists the known names buried in the newer cemetery. A further page offers historical person research. I did not run any of the searches.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page, the research page and the Jewish cemetery page on 2026-11-08. No search run; the new virtual reading room was not opened.

providers.name: Stadtarchiv Nürnberg (Nuremberg city archive) - Hinweise für Familienforscher
providers.what: The Nuremberg city archive, whose family-research page lists the genealogical sources it holds. Some are available only by staff reply to a written enquiry: residents' registers, residents' registration cards, passport cards, grave and death cards, the registry office series and second copies of church books. In the reading room the address books for 1792 to 2002 (with gaps) and telephone books from 1936 are on the shelves, and screens search the holdings database by personal name. The page says family research is a private use and staff time is charged. Separate pages cover civil-register enquiries and historical registration enquiries. I did not see any online index or images.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archive home page and the family-research page on 2026-11-08. Online enquiry forms not opened.

providers.name: Stadtarchiv Stuttgart (city archive) - digitaler Lesesaal und Familienregister
providers.what: The Stuttgart city archive page links an online reading room (a findbuch.net catalogue), the digital Stuttgart city lexicon, and digitised Stuttgart material at the Württemberg State Library. It also offers downloadable forms for ordering copies from the family register and from the civil-status register, plus guide leaflets on the holdings and finding aids. I read only the link titles and PDF names, not the content of the catalogue, so I do not know which series have images or how a name search works.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archive page on 2026-11-08 and listed its links. The digital reading room and PDFs were not opened.

providers.name: Evangelisches Zentralarchiv in Berlin (EZA) - Kirchenbuchstelle für die Gebiete östlich von Oder und Neiße
providers.what: The central archive of the Evangelical Church in Germany, which also keeps church books from Protestant parishes east of the Oder and Neisse. Its family-research page counts about 6,000 church books from those parishes, about 750 military church books of the Prussian army and the Wehrmacht, about 70 from German Protestant congregations abroad, about 190 from the Leipe/Rippin area, and civil-status papers from former refugee and internment camps in Denmark. Most books can be read in the Berlin reading room (a fee of 9 euro a day for private research), on microfiche or digitally, and the larger part is on Archion, where the index is free and viewing images needs a paid registration. A province-by-province page explains survivals, for example that the Königsberg holdings are large but have few books after 1874. There is no general register, so the parish must be known. I did not open the book list.
providers.triageNote: Opened the family-research page, the provinces page, the viewing page and the online reading-room page on 2026-11-08. The list of church books and the archive catalogue were not opened. Existing row de-evangelisches-landeskirchliches-archiv-in-berlin is a different body; archion is the viewing portal.

providers.name: Bistumsarchiv Trier (Diocesan Archive) - Ahnenforschung
providers.what: The archive of the Catholic diocese of Trier explains how its church books and parish-family books serve genealogy. The page distinguishes official family books kept by priests (prescribed by the vicariate in 1905) from later compiled local family books. It says finding aids exist for the parish archives stored in the archive, sorted alphabetically by place, and that those already in digital form are on the archive's website. Entries to the end of 1899 are open, while later ones are closed, with closed parts of a book wrapped in paper bands. Researchers are expected to work independently and should order records in advance since some are in outstation stores. A reading-room booking calendar is linked. I did not open the finding-aid list, so I cannot say which parishes are included.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archive home page and the genealogy page on 2026-11-08. The finding-aid list and booking page were not opened.

providers.name: AGoFF - Arbeitsgemeinschaft ostdeutscher Familienforscher
providers.what: A society of more than 800 members worldwide researching families and regional history in the historic German settlement areas of central and eastern Europe. Its front page notes a finding aid for the NSDAP membership file held by the US National Archives, an index of East Prussian civilians deported by Russian forces in 1915 from a Russian Red Cross list, a Volhynia research group, and its book series, including a volume on citizenship grants in Kolberg 1559 to 1858. Regional databases are mentioned, with a note that surname searches are done in those, not the site search. Parts are for members only. I did not open the databases.
providers.triageNote: Opened the front page on 2026-11-08 and read the news items; the regional databases and members' area were not opened.

providers.name: Pommerscher Greif e.V. - Datenbanken (GreifX, Quellensuche)
providers.what: A society for Pomeranian family and local history. Its databases page describes GreifX, a central person index fed by members' indexing of Pomeranian church books and civil registers that can be searched freely by name and extra criteria. It also describes 'Quellensuche', a source finder for the whole historical Pomerania that shows where sources are held in archives, offices and online, links the finding aids (contents lists of online church books, indexing work, online local family books) and has a place directory. The society also publishes the Sedina archive. I did not run a search in either database.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the databases page on 2026-11-08. The two databases were not opened.

providers.name: VFFOW - Verein für Familienforschung in Ost- und Westpreußen
providers.what: A society for family research in East and West Prussia. Its menu lists research aids (first steps, old handwriting, a place finder for East and West Prussia, administrative divisions, archive information for German, Polish and Russian archives), a databases section including an East and West Prussia researchers' file and an indexing project for Protestant church books, news and events. The EZA Berlin church-book page also points researchers to it for jurisdictions. I opened the home page and the indexing-project page only as far as the menus, so I do not know how many entries the databases hold or who can search them.

providers.name: Digitale Bibliothek Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
providers.what: A cross-sector portal of digitised holdings from archives, libraries, museums and university collections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, offered free for private and scholarly use, built on Goobi viewer. The home page lists recent imports (on the day, early printed funeral and wedding poems in Latin) and offers browsing by place of publication, creator and title. For genealogists the early funeral and wedding occasional prints and local printed works are the likely material; I did not look for registers or newspapers. I did not run a search.

providers.name: sachsen.digital - Portal für das digitalisierte Kulturerbe Sachsens
providers.what: The Saxon portal for digitised cultural heritage, bringing together libraries, archives, museums and other institutions. The home page says it offers one search across metadata and full text and counts more than 134,000 titles in the whole collection; its featured item is a collection of historic letterheads of Saxon firms from a Saxon business archive. It describes open access to sources for research and education. I did not run a search or check which newspapers, address books or registers are included.

providers.name: Friedhöfe Wien - Verstorbenensuche (burial search)
providers.what: The deceased-persons search of Friedhöfe Wien, the Vienna cemetery operator. Its page says the search finds details of all people buried in the cemeteries run by the company, with the exception of the denominational cemeteries, and a search starts from the criteria entered and a click on the magnifier beside the name. The Vienna history wiki lists this tool among its research aids. It is therefore a lead for grave location and burial dates in Vienna's municipal cemeteries, not for church or Jewish burial grounds. I did not run a search, so the fields shown for a hit and the period covered are not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08 and read the description. No search run.

providers.name: Wien Geschichte Wiki (City of Vienna history wiki)
providers.what: The historical knowledge platform of the City of Vienna, based on a historical lexicon of Vienna and growing through contributors. On the day I looked it counted 52,652 articles, 303,728 addresses and 23,029 images. Its front page groups content by people, places, buildings, organisations, events, memorials and maps, and has a section on Jewish communities and on source studies. A list of research tools includes a street-name lexicon, the deceased search, house-numbering history, courts by district and building records. For family historians the address entries, house-numbering history and street lexicon help interpret addresses in old records. I did not look at an individual article.
providers.triageNote: Opened the main page on 2026-11-08 and read the counts and the tool list; no article opened.

providers.name: Familia Austria - Österreichische Gesellschaft für Genealogie und Geschichte

The page is translated into many languages including Hungarian, Czech, Polish, Ukrainian, Romanian, Croatian, Slovak, Slovenian, Serbian, Italian, Hebrew, French, Spanish and English. Members can log in. Gatherings listed include research evenings and meetings with Hungarian-German researchers. I did not open the data collections, so I cannot say what is searchable without membership.

providers.name: Vorarlberger Landesarchiv - Online-Lesesaal und Personenstandsbücher
